files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,212 @@
+name: Build 3.1.3 MMCE and scan hotfixes
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: build-v3.1.3-scan-hotfix
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 50
+    env:
+      BASE_SHA: 9c5be408df787000a7e650f66f0a43411060e1d7
+      FRONTEND_BASE_SHA: 127d012b07322dc0805ce62f877e5ba5e8cd6dbc
+      FRONTEND_SHA: a288a1c4423625ae53d645ff0c46df92daea314d
+      MMCE_SHA: 0e78d1b35c71d1ee43b880c433586d830249b6f0
+      CORE_SHA: 360a788ff7bb7c6853702a8edec6860cae49c0a2
+      ORIGINAL_SHA256: cb07cd7079b8f39f9a7197d0d3c8937c4c51a5dcabf376a5fe159cfcc6e7318e
+      BUILD_IMAGE: ps2max/dev@sha256:e390699d46818e7c736f414ae5b1789d3ef7d3d914ce646a8a7bd027bd7e4521
+    steps:
+      - name: Check out the original 3.1.3 source
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
+        with:
+          ref: 9c5be408df787000a7e650f66f0a43411060e1d7
+          path: release
+          fetch-depth: 1
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Select the isolated frontend containing only the two hotfixes
+        working-directory: release
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$BASE_SHA"
+          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD:nhddl)" = "$FRONTEND_BASE_SHA"
+          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD:psxcore)" = "$CORE_SHA"
+          git submodule update --init --recursive nhddl psxcore
+          git -C nhddl fetch --depth=1 origin "$FRONTEND_SHA"
+          git -C nhddl checkout --detach "$FRONTEND_SHA"
+          test "$(git -C nhddl/iop/mmceman rev-parse HEAD)" = "$MMCE_SHA"
+          test "$(git -C psxcore rev-parse HEAD)" = "$CORE_SHA"
+          test -z "$(git -C nhddl status --porcelain)"
+          test -z "$(git -C psxcore status --porcelain)"
+          python3 - <<'PY'
+          import os
+          import subprocess
+          expected = {
+              'include/devices/devices.h', 'include/storage.h',
+              'iop/mmceman-eof.cmake', 'irx.cmake', 'src/devices/iso.c',
+              'src/storage.c', 'src/ui/file_manager.c', 'src/ui/language_catalog.inc',
+          }
+          changed = subprocess.check_output([
+              'git', '-C', 'nhddl', 'diff', '--name-only',
+              os.environ['FRONTEND_BASE_SHA'], os.environ['FRONTEND_SHA'],
+          ], text=True).splitlines()
+          assert set(changed) == expected, changed
+          subprocess.run(['git', '-C', 'nhddl', 'diff', '--check',
+                          os.environ['FRONTEND_BASE_SHA'], os.environ['FRONTEND_SHA']], check=True)
+          print('Verified exact eight-file hotfix scope. Core, SDK and other engines unchanged.')
+          PY
+
+      - name: Download and verify the original package
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          gh release download v3.1.3 --repo dnunezx/LUNA \
+            --pattern LUNA-v3.1.3-FMCB-mc0.zip --dir original
+          printf '%s  %s\n' "$ORIGINAL_SHA256" original/LUNA-v3.1.3-FMCB-mc0.zip | sha256sum -c -
+
+      - name: Build the hardware launcher against the original core
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          docker run --rm -v "$PWD/release:/workspace" \
+            -e LUNA_BUILD_IMAGE="$BUILD_IMAGE" "$BUILD_IMAGE" sh -eu -c '
+              if [ ! -e "$PS2SDK/ps2dev.cmake" ]; then
+                ln -s ../share/ps2dev.cmake "$PS2SDK/ps2dev.cmake"
+              fi
+              export LUNA_BUILD_DIR=/workspace/nhddl/build-v3.1.3-hotfix2
+              export LUNA_EMULATOR_OPTION=OFF
+              export LUNA_PSXCORE_DEVELOPMENT=OFF
+              sh /workspace/tools/bootstrap-ps2-libtiff.sh
+              cmake -S /workspace/nhddl -B "$LUNA_BUILD_DIR" \
+                -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DENABLE_PRINTF=OFF \
+                -DLUNA_RELEASE_VERSION=v3.1.3 -DLUNA_EMULATOR_BUILD=OFF \
+                -DLUNA_ENABLE_PSXCORE=ON -DLUNA_PSXCORE_DEVELOPMENT=OFF \
+                -DLUNA_PSXCORE_SOURCE_DIR=/workspace/psxcore
+              sh /workspace/tools/build-luna-psxcore.sh
+            '
+
+      - name: Package only the updated launcher and verify every other file
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          python3 - <<'PY'
+          from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
+          import hashlib
+          import os
+          import re
+          import subprocess
+          import zipfile
+
+          source = Path('release')
+          build = source / 'nhddl/build-v3.1.3-hotfix2'
+          original = Path('original/LUNA-v3.1.3-FMCB-mc0.zip')
+          output = Path('output')
+          output.mkdir()
+          sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+          def git(directory, *args):
+              return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(directory), *args], text=True).strip()
+          for directory, expected in (
+              (source, os.environ['BASE_SHA']),
+              (source / 'nhddl', os.environ['FRONTEND_SHA']),
+              (source / 'nhddl/iop/mmceman', os.environ['MMCE_SHA']),
+              (source / 'psxcore', os.environ['CORE_SHA']),
+          ):
+              assert git(directory, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD') == expected
+          assert git(source / 'nhddl', 'status', '--porcelain') == ''
+          assert git(source / 'nhddl/iop/mmceman', 'status', '--porcelain') == ''
+          assert git(source / 'psxcore', 'status', '--porcelain') == ''
+          assert sha(original.read_bytes()) == os.environ['ORIGINAL_SHA256']
+          prefix = 'LUNA-v3.1.3-FMCB-mc0/'
+          with zipfile.ZipFile(original) as archive:
+              assert archive.testzip() is None
+              names = [i.filename for i in archive.infolist() if not i.is_dir()]
+              assert len(names) == len(set(names))
+              assert all(n.startswith(prefix) and '..' not in PurePosixPath(n).parts for n in names)
+              files = {n: archive.read(n) for n in names}
+          previous = files.copy()
+          manifest = prefix + 'SHA256SUMS.txt'
+          for line in files[manifest].decode('ascii').splitlines():
+              digest, relative = line.split('  ', 1)
+              assert sha(files[prefix + relative]) == digest
+          metadata = (build / 'psxcore-build.txt').read_text()
+          for flag in ('emulator_build=OFF', 'development=OFF',
+                       'runtime_source=matching-checkout', 'igr_return=ON',
+                       'disc_swapping=ON', 'igr_return_path=mc0:/APP_LUNA/luna.elf',
+                       'psxcore_revision=' + os.environ['CORE_SHA'],
+                       'frontend_revision=' + os.environ['FRONTEND_SHA'],
+                       'frontend_dirty=no'):
+              assert flag in metadata.splitlines(), flag
+          cache = (build / 'CMakeCache.txt').read_text()
+          for key, value in (('ENABLE_PRINTF', 'OFF'), ('CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE', 'Release'),
+                             ('LUNA_EMULATOR_BUILD', 'OFF'), ('LUNA_ENABLE_PSXCORE', 'ON'),
+                             ('LUNA_PSXCORE_DEVELOPMENT', 'OFF'), ('LUNA_RELEASE_VERSION', 'v3.1.3')):
+              assert re.search(r'^' + key + r':[^=]+=' + value + '$', cache, re.MULTILINE), key
+          for line in (build / 'psxcore-build.sha256').read_text().splitlines():
+              digest, relative = line.split('  ', 1)
+              assert sha((build / relative).read_bytes()) == digest
+          launcher = prefix + 'APP_LUNA/luna.elf'
+          files[launcher] = (build / 'luna.elf').read_bytes()
+          metadata += (
+              '\nrelease_version=v3.1.3\n'
+              'release_variant=hotfix2: MMCE EOF and tolerant scan recovery\n'
+              'base_revision=' + os.environ['BASE_SHA'] + '\n'
+              'frontend_base_revision=' + os.environ['FRONTEND_BASE_SHA'] + '\n'
+              'mmceman_revision=' + os.environ['MMCE_SHA'] + '\n'
+              'runtime_packaging=original-release-byte-identical\n'
+              'original_package_sha256=' + os.environ['ORIGINAL_SHA256'] + '\n'
+          )
+          files[prefix + 'BUILD-INFO.txt'] = metadata.encode()
+          files[manifest] = ''.join(
+              f'{sha(data)}  {name[len(prefix):]}\n'
+              for name, data in sorted(files.items()) if name != manifest
+          ).encode('ascii')
+          changed = {n for n in files if files[n] != previous[n]}
+          expected = {launcher, prefix + 'BUILD-INFO.txt', manifest}
+          assert set(files) == set(previous) and changed == expected, changed
+          # The original runtime/module list is the package allowlist.
+          assert files[prefix + 'APP_LUNA/psxcore-runtime-bootstrap.elf'] == previous[prefix + 'APP_LUNA/psxcore-runtime-bootstrap.elf']
+          for name in files:
+              parts = PurePosixPath(name).parts
+              assert not any(p.lower() in {'tests', 'fixtures', 'local', 'diagnostics', 'psxcore-tester'} for p in parts)
+              assert PurePosixPath(name).suffix.lower() not in {'.map', '.log', '.o', '.a', '.exe', '.py', '.sh', '.c', '.h'}
+          archive_path = output / 'LUNA-v3.1.3-hotfix2-FMCB-mc0.zip'
+          with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=9) as archive:
+              for name, data in sorted(files.items()):
+                  archive.writestr(name, data)
+          with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
+              assert archive.testzip() is None
+              assert all(archive.read(n) == data for n, data in files.items())
+          (output / 'LUNA-v3.1.3-hotfix2.elf').write_bytes(files[launcher])
+          (output / 'BUILD-INFO.txt').write_text(metadata)
+          checksums = ''.join(f'{sha(p.read_bytes())}  {p.name}\n' for p in sorted(output.iterdir()))
+          (output / 'SHA256SUMS.txt').write_text(checksums, encoding='ascii')
+          summary = (
+              '## LUNA 3.1.3 — two hotfixes only\n\n'
+              'Includes MMCE directory-end handling and tolerant library scan recovery.\n\n'
+              f'Frontend: `{os.environ["FRONTEND_SHA"]}` based on the original 3.1.3 frontend.\n\n'
+              'Only the launcher ELF, build metadata and checksums differ from the original package. '
+              'All runtimes, modules, settings and license files are byte-identical.\n\n'
+              'Physical MMCE/gameplay testing remains. The public release and tag were not changed.\n'
+          )
+          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY'], 'a') as report:
+              report.write(summary)
+          print(summary)
+          PY
+
+      - name: Upload downloadable build files
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
+        with:
+          name: LUNA-v3.1.3-hotfix2-${{ github.run_number }}
+          path: output/*
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          retention-days: 30

Recover stable dashboard feedback and localize core UI in nine languages

Preserve staged copy recovery while resolving ambiguous legacy stat results and MCMAN creation flags. Restore transfer layout, viewport synchronization and Neutrino option audio; omit offscreen carousel cards. Append dashboard labels to all nine language tables with focused regression coverage.

Generate githash.h before CI target builds so ignored headers cannot misidentify the recovery artifacts. Verify stale-header replacement and unchanged reruns.

fix: reject unsafe external dashboard format overrides
test: cover translation format injection and native MC O_EXCL handling

test: exercise MC-to-MMCE and cross-device paste with EISDIR stat faults

Restore stat-only FatFs error normalization lost in baseline recovery. Confirm card lookup success through parent entries and exercise raw status failures before writes.

Co-authored-by: OpenAI ChatGPT <noreply@openai.com>

Restore upstream R3Z direct file overwrite behavior

Remove destination stat and enumeration preflight, staging, checksums, backup/rename publication and their status/flag workarounds. Keep dashboard presentation and existing device/source integration. Replace transaction tests with direct-copy compatibility coverage.

Co-authored-by: OpenAI ChatGPT <noreply@openai.com>

Use upstream single-call read/write dispatch, original buffer sizing and close-error output retention. Keep dashboard presentation, source checks, device support and dedicated backup/recovery features. Verify cut/move source deletion follows successful copy only.

Correct release wording, localize section keys and reject unrelated parent-checkout build identities. Add focused regression coverage and brace the MMCE pathname guards.

 ## Rolling
 
-- **Infinite list navigation wrap-around:** dashboard lists now cycle at boundaries (up from first selects last, down from last selects first), including File Browser views, app/library lists, Files/Devices pickers, Tools, Settings and HDD Manager.
-- **Safer file replacement:** an existing destination is retained until its replacement has been written and checked. Failed publication rolls back; recovery files survive interrupted operations.
-- **Copy failure details:** compact stage/error, device, byte-count and build information make failed transfers diagnosable. A failed source-folder listing is no longer reported as an empty successful copy.
-- **Cross-device copying:** positive short reads and writes complete the remaining bytes. Slot-2 card preparation happens before opening source files when leaving MX4SIO.
-- **Clearer file operations:** the dashboard shows the filename, remaining megabytes and a progress bar while copying, with progress updates during deletion and verification.
-- **Release-page clarity:** the public release page now includes a concise Rolling changelog summary and links directly to full release notes and changelog history.
-- **Consistent storage names:** Home and the application library use MASS labels for mass-storage applications.
-- **Software clock:** setting a time now offers to save it immediately and waits for verified storage completion. Save current clock retains later runtime. The clock resumes the saved checkpoint after restart; elapsed time while unplugged is unavailable.
-- **Storage loading:** returned mount waits redraw more frequently while retaining the existing device discovery windows. MMCE returns each probed port's bus state to the normal card/controller drivers.
-- **Power-off:** setup starts only the power-off service, without loading unused DEV9 drivers, and detects failed initialization.
+- **Dashboard languages:** navigation, Settings labels, common actions and transfer progress use the nine built-in language tables. External LNG overrides also apply to these labels. User filenames, paths and application metadata keep their original text; some extended help remains in English.
+- **File-copy compatibility:** restore upstream wLaunchELF_R3Z direct overwrite behavior. Remove the custom destination-stat, staging, verification, backup and rename transaction so ordinary paste does not depend on those additional operations.
+- **Clearer file operations:** copy/delete popups give filenames their own full-width row, show remaining MB or completed selected items, and finish with a full progress bar. Paste failures include a readable reason, stage and numeric error.
+- **Navigation and rendering:** wrapped list selections stay visible in the new viewport. Carousel rendering omits fully offscreen cards while retaining visible geometry and order. Physical-console acceptance remains unverified.
+- **Neutrino options:** menu audio stays active until launch is committed, with ordinary ELF muting and failure recovery preserved.
+- **Retained improvements:** concise release notes, dashboard free-space display, MASS display names, verified software-clock saves, lazy storage loading and power-off service initialization remain available.
 
 ## Earlier changes

+

Existing untracked work/build directories are retained. No hardware report is automatically closed and no release is published by this branch.

Native-language and target-font/layout review pending. |
+
+## Upstream file-handling restoration
+
+On 2026-10-25 the maintainer explicitly requested upstream wLaunchELF_R3Z file handling and removal of the custom replacement transaction. This supersedes the earlier staged-replacement design and validation notes.
+
+Reference: saildot4k/wLaunchELF_R3Z master `06b06d000072d358c93d98104d64d2f081e47ba7`, `src/filer_copy.c` and `src/filer_fileops.c`.
+
+Normal and recursive file replacement now use the upstream operation sequence: `genRemove(out)`, then `genOpen(out, FIO_O_WRONLY | FIO_O_TRUNC | FIO_O_CREAT)`, transfer and close. No destination-stat preflight, parent-directory scan, exclusive-create flag, sibling staging file, checksum verification, backup publication or rename is required. Remove the FatFs stat reinterpretation introduced for that transaction; `genGetStat` again passes through driver results. Existing device-path integration remains.
+
+The dashboard progress/error presentation, worker/device preparation, source handling and supported-device metadata dispatch remain integrated. The follow-up restores upstream's single read/write per chunk, buffer sizing, and retention of the output after close failure. Custom short-I/O completion loops and the dashboard-specific MC/VMC buffer cap are removed. Same-path protection avoids deleting the source. MMCE's unsupported timestamp operation is skipped. No user firmware change is required by copying or replacement.
+
+Scope: normal copy/move/delete/rename, folders, metadata and their dashboard call paths. The inherited rename/delete operations remain in use; cut/move deletes its source only after successful copying. Preserve CF/i.Link support, driver lifecycle coordination, launcher handoffs, timestamp-editor UI, backup/history/recovery features, translations and dashboard rendering. This correction does not revert those features or claim their complete source identity with upstream.
+
+Direct replacement has upstream's failure behavior: once the old destination is removed, a failed copy does not retain the original. There is no automatic backup or rollback promise. Existing unrelated backup/history features are unchanged.
+
+## Localization contract
+
+IDs 0-467 retain their order and content. New IDs are appended to all nine tables with matching format signatures. Older external LNG files inherit built-in defaults for appended IDs. Missing/empty resolver values fall back to source text. Static UI metadata retains source labels rather than pointers into a replaceable external language buffer.
+
+The renderer is unchanged. User filenames, application metadata, bookmarks, paths, config keys, protocol tokens, custom theme names and native language names remain outside automatic translation. Catalogs follow the existing ASCII convention. Untranslated extended help is disclosed and is not counted as completed coverage.
+
+## Validation
+
+CI includes the overlay, Neutrino-audio, carousel-culling and language fixtures alongside the existing host suite. Copy cases cover repeated direct overwrite, smaller and empty replacements, cross-device MC/MMCE/USB copies, source failures, write/close failures and recursive directories. Destination stat and rename adapters abort if unexpectedly called. POSIX filesystem fixtures run under WSL/Ubuntu rather than Windows MinGW.
+
+Host regressions, standard/DS34 builds, controller/UDPFS checks, loader layout and package verification are distinct evidence layers. No emulator or physical console result is claimed. Keep #187 and #198 open pending the affected-runtime report.

+"""Stamp ps2build artifacts with this checkout's committed source identity."""
+import argparse
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+
+
+def revision():
+    top = subprocess.run(['git', 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'],
+                         cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
+    if top.returncode or Path(top.stdout.strip()).resolve() != ROOT.resolve():
+        return None
+    result = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', '-s', '--format=%H%n%cs', 'HEAD'],
+                            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
+    lines = result.stdout.splitlines()
+    if result.returncode or len(lines) != 2:
+        return None
+    sha, date = lines
+    if not re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{40}', sha) or not re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', date):
+        return None
+    return sha[:12], date
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=ROOT / 'githash.h')
+    parser.add_argument('--require-git', action='store_true')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    identity = revision()
+    if identity is None and args.require_git:

@@ -1,5 +1,205 @@
 # RIPPS2 changelog
 
+## Build 114 (beta, v1.1.4-beta when released), changes since build 113
+
+The user's plans of 10/22: All Games before the drives answer, hide and delete games, the launchers found and
+remembered, a smaller ELF for memory cards, and the field reports from FifthFox (iLink, size) and Berion (APA). And of
+10/23: launches that never run into RIPPS2's own reading and writing, every settings page on one screen, one HDD, new
+Color Themes and the Color Sweep, and one newer Roboto with weights. Then: a theme list on the SELECT hold, games
+compressed to ZSO and back, a launch guard that only shows when a wait is long, and RiptOPL's guarded exFAT driver.
+
+### RiptOPL brought up to date
+- **RiptOPL rebuild/main 57c45b4 merged** (192 commits since 3cd7f89): i.LINK logs back in after an IOP reset and
+  RiptOPL's i.LINK driver rides with Neutrino and POPSTARTER (#1018, FifthFox's iLink report), the in-game menu
+  from the VBLANK handler (#984), **compatibility Mode 8, Slow Reads** (#924: Accurate Reads at the CD rate for DVD
+  games, OPL core only, ripto's fix for games that fail on fast reads), the USB / MX4SIO / iLink discovery waits skipped, VMC and ZSO fixes, Ember's
+  starting disc from discs.txt, and the translation format checks. RIPPS2's own sound voices, in-game menu and
+  keyed language files kept their build 104 to 113 behaviour on top.
+
+### All Games, whole from the first frame
+- **The master list.** Every game All Games lists is kept in `allgames.bin` beside the settings (mc0:/RIPPS2, or
+  where Save Settings To points). At boot All Games shows all of them at once: a game whose drive has not answered
+  yet is listed and waits for it, and is swapped for the real row the moment its drive's list comes in.
+- **Drives on Manual stay instant.** Their games are listed too; Cross on one starts its drive, waits for its list
+  and launches the game. A drive that is turned off, or started and silent for 40 seconds, drops its saved games.
+- Written in place only when the list changed and no started drive is still to answer, never with Write
+  Operations or Fast Cache off; a short or damaged file is ignored, never half read.
+
+### The launchers you keep, found once
+- **RIPPS2 searches the started drives** for POPSTARTER, the POPS files, Ember, Ember's BIOS and Neutrino and
+  remembers where each one is, by drive kind (`launchers.txt` beside the settings). Every launch reads them from
+  there after the places RIPPS2 always looked, and every launch that finds one notes it.
+- **Settings > Game Sources > Cache** shows each of the five as found (and where) or not found yet, with **Look
+  now**. A launch that finds none offers the search, and the place found is kept for every launch after.
+- **Ember** needs its files beside the games: when RIPPS2 knows a copy elsewhere, START copies Ember (or its BIOS)
+  there and starts the game. **RIPPOPS** copies the POPS files from where RIPPS2 found them. Both copy with the
+  RIPPS2 progress bar (compression's panel), where they showed one still line for seconds.
+- **Neutrino** is looked for at Settings' path, on the game's drive, on the memory cards and on every started
+  drive before anything is offered; RIPPS2's own 1.8.0 is offered once, only when none is found anywhere.
+
+### STATUS: drives first
+- **DRIVES** opens the page: every started drive by kind, the internal HDD (APA)'s free space, each memory card's
+  free KB, the MMCE card, and what is off. **START EVERY DRIVE** starts the rest.
+- **LAUNCHERS**: one line each for Neutrino, POPSTARTER, the POPS files, Ember and Ember's BIOS, and **LOOK FOR
+  THEM** (it can start every drive first). Then the homebrew and BIBLE as before. The page is now titled Drives,
+  launchers and homebrew.
+
+### Hide a game
+- **Hide Game** in a game's Triangle options (on All Games and Starred Games rows too): the game leaves every list,
+  All Games, Starred Games, Recents and Random Game included. The hidden list is kept on the game's own drive
+  (`RIPPS2.HID` beside RIPPS2.LST), so it travels with the drive.
+- **Settings > Game Sources > Hidden Games** lists every started drive's hidden games: Show Again, or Delete.
+
+### Delete a game completely
+- **Delete** now takes everything of the game's: every part of the image (ul.cfg rebuilt for a UL game), its CFG,
+  its art and its cheats; on the internal HDD (APA) its partition, then its CFG, art and cheats in +OPL. Delete
+  works on APA games, All Games and Starred Games rows (found on their drive at that moment), and hidden games.
+- **Saves stay unless you say.** Its VMC, POPSTARTER saves and RIPSHOT pictures are kept unless you answer Yes,
+  and a CFG or art another copy of the game still uses is kept and named. A last screen only START gets past.
+- **Berion's APA check.** Before any partition goes (the HDD MANAGER's remove too), RIPPS2 walks the whole table:
+  every header's magic and checksum, each link forward and back, every partition inside this disk, no size or
+  alignment this disk cannot have, the chain closing at __mbr. A table written from an image of another disk size
+  is refused with the reason, and nothing is touched. The walk runs again after, and `REMOVED.TXT` in mc0:/RIPPS2
+  keeps what went, from where, the space freed and the table's state.
+
+### A smaller RIPPS2.elf
+- **One ELF, as before**, carrying BIBLE and Neutrino; POPSTARTER and Ember are found where you keep them, as
+  since build 113. It is about 26 KB smaller than v1.1.3 with everything above in it: FreeType is started with only
+  the modules RIPPS2 reads (TrueType, sfnt, the autohinter, the smooth renderer, CFF), so Type 1, CID, PFR, BDF,
+  PCF, WinFNT, SDF and SVG leave the link, and the built-in fonts lose glyph names, extra name records and
+  substitution tables (render-checked identical at 14 to 32 px).
+
+### Safe launches, and the launch guard
+- **No write runs into a launch.** FifthFox lost two card images and a USB stick, likely to a write cut by a launch's
+  reset. A launch now stops RIPPS2's background writes the moment the game is picked (RIPPS2.LST, allgames.bin, the
+  hidden lists, art, RIPSHOT, the games list cache), waits for one already started, and stops a drive's list read at its
+  next entry.
+- **Big writes start in step with the drive.** In the lab, a big write that started at an odd place in a file and ran
+  across a 32 KB cluster now and then landed a cluster too early on exFAT, and the file's chain broke after it (found on
+  a compressed game, studied on the PC). RIPPS2.LST, the list cache every started drive keeps since build 110, had that
+  shape once a library's list passed one cluster: it is now one write from the file's start. Compression, RIPDISC's raw
+  and audio rips, RIPSHOT's pictures and BIOS Music's WAV now write whole 256 KB pieces at multiples of it.
+- **Every drive known for what it is.** RiptOPL's exFAT/FAT driver, as RIPPS2 builds it, now says a drive's format,
+  cluster size and free space. STATUS shows them for every USB, MX4SIO, iLink and exFAT HDD drive. RIPDISC checks the
+  room before a rip, and a game over 4 GB goes in 1 GB parts only on a drive that really is FAT32: an exFAT stick takes
+  the ISO whole (before, the PS2 could not tell, so every drive but the internal HDD got parts). Memory Files checks the
+  room and FAT32's 4 GB a file before a copy, and copies files over 2 GB right (a 32-bit count failed its own check).
+  Compression, rips and copies write in whole clusters of the drive.
+- **MMCE: mmceman brought up to ps2-mmce's main** (de28936f): its hook no longer blocks the second memory card port,
+  which only MX4SIO needed. Compressing on an MMCE card renames the finished image into place, which sd2psXtd does from
+  firmware 1.4.0 on. **Hotfix (10/24):** on an MMCE card RIPPS2 first writes and renames a tiny file beside the game, so
+  older firmware is told in a second to update ([sd2psxtd.github.io/download](https://sd2psxtd.github.io/download)), with nothing changed, instead of
+  after the whole work.
+- **One background write at a time.** RIPPS2's own background writes now wait for each other (about 3 seconds at most;
+  one that cannot wait is simply written next time), and none starts while Memory Files pastes, unpacks or deletes,
+  while RIPDISC rips, or while a game is compressed.
+- **RiptOPL's guarded exFAT driver.** RIPPS2 shipped the SDK's stock exFAT/FAT driver; it now ships the one RiptOPL's
+  own releases build. A game on a damaged FAT chain is refused at launch (#986) instead of handing the game's
+  driver wrong sectors to write its VMC to, and the merged RiptOPL's new VMC maker can reserve a card in one piece on
+  USB and the other BDM drives (with the stock driver it refused).
+- **The launch guard.** A game picked while RIPPS2 is still reading a drive or saving a list waits its turn: a glass
+  panel fades in as RIPDISC's does, names what RIPPS2 is finishing, and RIPDISC's notches fill toward when it will be
+  done (each drive's last list read is timed). The game starts by itself when the work is done. **START NOW** stops
+  the work safely and starts at once; **Back** returns to the page the launch began on, unchanged. Music plays on.
+- **Only when it is needed.** A wait of a second or two shows the loading icon over the page and nothing else; the
+  panel fades in when the work will take longer, or has run past what it was expected to take.
+
+### Settings, every page on one screen
+- **Game Sources**: the BDM drives (USB, MX4SIO, PC Card, DESR, iLink) on a **BDM Devices** page of their own; the
+  greyed Protocol row gone (the Network page has it). **Interface**: Video Mode, Widescreen, H-POS, V-POS and Overscan
+  on a **Screen** page; VCD Games List Settings on PS Emulation only. **Flow and Grid** is **Layout**, with the
+  category rows; **Colors and More** is **Colors and Text**, with **Text Weight**. Network keeps its rows and scrolls.
+- The hub's names are shorter (PS Emulation, Controllers, Audio); General & System has its title; the POPSTARTER
+  network page has one name and a notice that fits; the VCD list's label lines up; the Neutrino arguments page has
+  its row's name; MMCE says On and Off; STATUS's BIBLE line fits; Artwork Settings gets **Missing Covers** (the Network
+  page keeps its Cover Art download too); a game's options end with one **Achievements** row that opens the three.
+
+### One HDD
+- A PS2 has one internal HDD, APA or exFAT. **HDD Start Mode** (Off, Manual, Auto) is the drive's, whatever its format,
+  and an exFAT drive no longer has an empty APA page beside it: Storage shows one HDD Games. An APA and exFAT hybrid
+  keeps both pages, named by format. **BDM Devices Start Mode** Off turns off the drives on the BDM Devices page
+  only: an exFAT internal HDD on Auto stays listed.
+- **Network Connectivity** Off on Game Sources turns the network page off again (since the Protocol row moved, it
+  had stayed in Storage until a restart).
+
+### Colors
+- **Color Theme** gains **Tangerine**, **Flamingo**, **Turquoise**, **Moonlight** (a ghostly white) and **Custom**:
+  the new **Theme Color** picker shows each theme's color and is yours to pick on Custom, as the text colors are.
+- **Color Sweep**: five colors the theme fades through, each for a few seconds, never fast enough to flash.
+  **Rainbow**, then a sweep made from each Color Theme (an all-pink Flamingo, a ghostly Moonlight). **Sweep Colors**
+  opens its five pickers and its speed (Slow, Normal, Lively), seen live; change one of RIPPS2's and it is kept as
+  your own, under the name you give it (up to four; left as it is, "Rainbow" becomes "Rainbow 2").
+- **Color Sweep, kinder**: a speed picked for one of RIPPS2's sweeps is kept as that sweep's own (no copy under a new
+  name; a copy is made only when its colours change), and your own sweeps can be deleted (Sweep Colors > Delete This
+  Sweep). While a sweep is on, Color Theme greys out and says Sweep, and the Theme Color box beside it shows plain
+  grey; your Color Theme is kept and comes back when the sweep is Off.
+- **The notch panels line up**: RIPDISC, the launch guard and compression share one frame, the same width and place,
+  with the same wheel.
+
+### The theme list
+- **Hold SELECT** on a game list opens your themes in a glass panel, eight to a page, in the Settings font: pick one and
+  the panel fades out and the theme loads (the one in use just refreshes the page). The built-in themes (RIPPS2, RIPFLOW,
+  RIPGRID) come first, together, then the themes on your drives, in every theme list. **Settings > Interface > Hold
+  SELECT**: List (the default), Cycle (the next theme, as before) or Off.
+
+### Hide Game and Compression
+- A game's Triangle options say **Hide Game and Compression** for an ISO or ZSO (USB, MX4SIO, iLink, the exFAT HDD,
+  MMCE), named either way (Name.iso, or OPL Manager's SCUS_XXX.XX.Name.iso): **Hide Game** as before, **Compress to
+  ZSO** (the game stays in your lists), **Hide and Compress** (hidden once the ZSO is made and checked; a cancel or a
+  failure hides nothing), or for a ZSO **Uncompress to ISO**.
+- **Room first.** Before anything starts, the drive is asked for its free space: the new image needs about the old one's
+  size beside it while it works (the original stays to the end). Short of room, it says how much is needed and how much
+  is free, and nothing changes. (RiptOPL's exFAT/FAT driver, as RIPPS2 builds it, now answers that question; MMCE cannot
+  say, and there the work stops cleanly if the drive fills.)
+- **Experimental, and asked twice**: a panel with RIPDISC's notches shows the game, its size, its drive and about how
+  long it takes, and fills while you hold SELECT; then a second yes. A RIPPS2 progress bar runs the whole way
+  (COMPRESSING 1 OF 2, 2 OF 2, CHECKING EVERY PIECE) with CANCEL, which removes what was written. In the lab a 1.2 GB
+  game on the internal exFAT HDD took about 10 minutes and came out 82% of its size; the first estimate is set from
+  that, and the bar's own estimate follows what it really gets.
+- **Nothing is lost.** The ISO stays until the ZSO has been read back and every piece checked against it, and only then
+  does RIPPS2 ask before removing it (Circle reads **Back (keeps both)** there: the ISO and the ZSO both stay). The lab showed why the check is there: written in pieces of any length, the
+  driver now and then put a 32 KB cluster over the one before it, and the check caught it every time. The new image now
+  goes to the drive in whole aligned 256 KB pieces, as RIPDISC's rips and Memory Files' copies always did. The ZSO starts with the OPL core (Neutrino does not read ZSO); its VMC, settings,
+  art and cheats are the same game's. Uncompress makes the ISO again the same way.
+- **Hidden Games too**: Settings > Game Sources > Hidden Games offers Compress to ZSO (or Uncompress to ISO) beside
+  Show Again and Delete, and marks a compressed one PS2 ZSO. A hidden game stays hidden once compressed.

RIPPS2's own code, written from the formats. - [ps2sdk](https://github.com/ps2dev/ps2sdk) by the ps2dev team: the memory card file system (mcman) and the USB keyboard driver.

+His setup: SCPH-39001; slot 1 MMCE (its card images, .MCD, on its own SD card), slot 2 MX4SIO, USB, iLink (FAT32,

+
+What the code does (read 10/23, nothing run yet):
+- A launch's teardown (deinitEx) waits for the IO worker at most LAUNCH_IO_DRAIN_TICKS, about 10 s, then goes on;
+  ioEnd() only raises a flag. The worker keeps running the request in hand, and the queue behind it, while the
+  launch unmounts and resets the IOP.
+- A scan of a slow drive (MMCE libraries take minutes; FifthFox's USB, MX4SIO and iLink are slow) easily outlasts
+  10 s, and RIPPS2's scans END IN A WRITE when the list changed: RIPPS2.LST on the drive itself (on an MMCE that is
+  mmce0:/, the SD card holding the .MCD files) since builds 109 and 110, and in 114 allgames.bin beside the settings
+  (mc0: on his console, which is the MMCE). Upstream's worker mostly reads, and a cut read is harmless; a cut write
+  leaves FAT or exFAT half updated. A launch that then stalls and is power-cycled does the same.

+# Discord website embed: boot to empty games
+
+This is a local preview of the website's existing Discord rich embed. It keeps the original title and description, uses the RIPPS2 brand icon, adds a general project introduction below the GIF, and provides Website, PSX-Place, GitHub, and guns.lol buttons. Nothing has been posted.
+
+## GIF sequence
+
+The loop uses a fresh launch of the RIPPS2 ELF in the isolated PCSX2 lab. It opens on the close tower animation, settles on the empty All Games list, pauses on the Start menu for about 10 seconds, then returns to the list before looping. It does not enter the Settings page. The capture shows 60 fps source video with no HDD error; the Discord GIF is 800 px wide at 12 fps to keep the full loop within a practical attachment size.
+
+## Lab and source capture
+
+- PCSX2 lab: `B:\Emulation\PlayStation\PCSX2\ripps2-lab-emptygames-capture`
+- ELF: `RIPPS2.elf` in the lab folder.
+- Virtual HDD: zero-filled `hdd-blank-2gb.raw`, enabled in this lab's `PCSX2.ini`.
+- Memory cards: lab scratch cards only; the user's original cards and reel disks are not used.
+- Source video: `videos\RIPPS2 [_]_RIPPS2_20261025000556.mp4`, 1920x1080, 60 fps, 28.05 seconds.
+- GIF: `media/b114/ripps2-boot-empty-games.gif`, 560x315, 12 fps, 28 seconds, 11,056,703 bytes.
+
+Recreate the GIF with:
+
+```powershell
+python tools/discord/make_boot_gif.py `
+  --video 'B:\Emulation\PlayStation\PCSX2\ripps2-lab-emptygames-capture\videos\RIPPS2 [_]_RIPPS2_20261025000556.mp4' `
+  --trim-start 0 --duration 28 --fps 12 --width 560 `
+  --out media/b114/ripps2-boot-empty-games.gif
+```
+
+## Preview files
+
+- `out/boot-empty-games/embed-preview.html` — rendered local preview.
+- `out/boot-empty-games/component-embed.json` — Discord Component Embed payload for review.
+- `out/boot-empty-games/ripps2-boot-empty-games.gif` — copied GIF attachment.
+- `tools/discord/make_boot_embed.py` — rebuilds the preview and payload from the website embed copy.
+
+## Website link preview
+
+`index.html` contains Discord's inline `<script id="discord:component-embed" type="application/json">` payload. Discord reads it when someone posts the website URL and renders the title, existing description, brand icon, GIF gallery, general introduction bullets, and four URL buttons as a Component Embed. The payload is under Discord's 3,000-byte limit. The Open Graph and Twitter tags remain as fallbacks.
+
+The Component Embed and GIF are published from `main` in commit `f0f0e8b`. GitHub Pages reports the build as complete. A live fetch using Discordbot's user agent returned the inline payload and the GIF with HTTP 200; the payload is 1,544 bytes and the GIF is 11,056,703 bytes. Component previews require Discord's crawler to reach the page and all media within 10 seconds; the GIF was reduced to 560x315 while retaining the 12 fps, 28-second sequence. The live asset fetched in about one second from the build host; Discord's Embed Debugger can be used to inspect the rendered card if needed.

commit.message: App icon
App icon

Console theme: models for 72 more systems, and four rebuilt

Each system's console as its card, built by Blender scripts in
tools/console-models/ (a layout, a Pillow print and the model per system),
measured from photographs and published dimensions, turned to a three-quarter
view, with an 8 s focused clip that plays a made-up game, Odyssey.

New: Amiga, ZX Spectrum, PlayStation, Super Nintendo, PlayStation 2, ZX81,
Nintendo DS, Nintendo 3DS, Satellaview, Wii, Atari 2600, MSX1, Apple II,
Master System, PICO-8, Atari ST, Nintendo 64, GameCube, 3DO, Famicom Disk
System, PC Engine, VIC-20, Neo Geo, ColecoVision, Flash, Mega-CD, Amiga CD32,
NAOMI, Apple IIGS, MSX2, CD-i, Wii U, Odyssey 2, Atari 5200, Atari Lynx,
Neo Geo CD, PC Engine CD, Neo Geo Pocket Color, Neo Geo Pocket,
PlayStation 3, Atari 7800, Watara Supervision, Atari Jaguar, Atari Jaguar CD,
PC-98, Xbox, Game & Watch, 32X, Vectrex, Pokémon mini, Virtual Boy,
GX4000, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360, PC-FX, Desktop Apps, PlayStation 5,
Intellivision, 64DD, Super Game Boy, BBC Micro, Acorn Electron, Atari 800,
Atari XE Game System, TI-99/4A, Channel F, Macintosh, CDTV, Plus/4,
Archimedes, Dragon 32 and Oric.

Rebuilt in the same style: Saturn, Dreamcast, NES (its door flips up and
out) and Mega Drive (with its pad, and an Odyssey label in place of a real
game's; the 32X's and Mega-CD's cards are unchanged).

Shared: plugs.py (each plugged-in cable ends in its real plug), controllers'
sides rounded outwards (the inset helpers' winding), one UV set per model.
CLAUDE.md, the decisions log and theme.toml updated to match.

Squashed from 86 commits on console-models.

Generated with Claude Code under company AI usage policy
Version 0.19.0

+"""The console theme's Amiga system model (godot/themes/console/models/systems/amiga.glb): an Amiga 500 and its
+Commodore 1084S monitor, Kickstart 1.3 asking for a disk.
+
+Built in Blender from the real machines' proportions (amiga_layout.py has the measurements, taken from photographs).
+The computer is its side outline extruded across its width: the keyboard deck rising from the low front edge, the step,
+the raised back rounding over at the back edge; nine vent grooves are cut across the raised back and the gaps of the
+comb of fins along its back edge, the keyboard's wells into the deck, and the drive's panel and slot into its right
+end. Its 96 keys (the UK layout) stand in the wells, tapering to their printed tops, off-white or grey as the real
+ones. Behind it stands the monitor: its side outline extruded (the hood sloping down behind), the bezel's panel sunk
+into its front, the screen's opening sloping in to the curved glass, its badge, the seams of the control flap under
+it, and a grille in each side. The printing is two textures drawn by amiga_print.py: the computer's top seen from above
+(planar-mapped onto every face facing up: the key tops and legends, the badge, the lights, the AMIGA lettering) with
+the monitor's badge and the swatches its bezel and the lit drive light take; and the screens (the glass at rest shows
+Kickstart 1.3's hand holding a disk), the floppy's two sides and their swatches.
+
+A node tree: a root (the turn to a three-quarter view, TILT_YAW and TILT_PITCH: the drive's end towards the viewer,
+the top tipped up; then the model spec's fit: standing on y = 0, centred, the largest side 1 m) holding the set; the
+set holding the floppy, the eject button, the lit drive light, two screens over the glass (black, and the title screen
+of a made-up game, Odyssey) and the Ctrl and Amiga keys. The floppy waits in the drive shrunk to nothing, the light and
+the screens are shrunk to nothing, so at rest the card is the set with Kickstart's hand on the screen.
+
+The `focused` clip (8 s, looping) loads a game: the floppy pops up beside the drive, flips over and slides in; the
+drive light flickers while the screen goes black, then Odyssey's title screen comes up. Ctrl and both Amiga keys go
+down together (the Amiga's reset), the hand is back, the eject button is pressed and the floppy pops out and goes.
+
+Seven materials (case, print, key_light, key_dark, dark, glass, disk) and two textures, within the system model
+budget. Run from the repo root:
+
+    python tools/console-models/amiga_print.py artifacts/amiga
+    blender -b --factory-startup --python tools/console-models/amiga.py -- artifacts/amiga godot/themes/console/models/systems/amiga.glb
+"""
+
+import math
+import os
+import sys
+
+import bmesh
+import bpy
+from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import amiga_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+from clip import HIDDEN, Pose, back_out, ease_in, ease_out, key, phase, smooth  # noqa: E402
+from mega_drive_cartridge import bevel, boolean, box, export, join, material, new_object, prism_x, triangles  # noqa: E402
+
+TILT_YAW = -30.0     # degrees about the vertical: the right end (the drive) comes towards the viewer
+TILT_PITCH = 25.0    # degrees about the horizontal: the top tips up towards the viewer
+ROUGHNESS = dict(case=0.55, print=0.55, key_light=0.5, key_dark=0.5, dark=0.8, glass=0.2, disk=0.4)
+RESET_KEYS = ("ctrl", "lamiga", "ramiga")
+
+# The deck's frame: x across, s up the slope from the deck's front edge, h off it.
+SLOPE_FRAME = Matrix.Translation((0.0, L.DECK[0][0], L.DECK[0][1])) @ Matrix.Rotation(L.SLOPE, 4, "X")
+PRESS = SLOPE_FRAME.to_3x3() @ Vector((0.0, 0.0, -1.0))   # a key's travel, in the model's frame
+
+
+# ---- UVs -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def atlas_uv(region, w, h):
+    """A face drawn w x h into region: (a, b) millimetres across it (a to the right, b down from its top) to UVs."""
+    rx, ry, rw, rh = region
+    return lambda a, b: ((rx + a / w * rw) / L.ATLAS, 1 - (ry + b / h * rh) / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+TOP = atlas_uv(L.PRINT_REGIONS["top"], L.WIDTH, L.DEPTH)
+
+
+def top_uv(co):
+    """The computer's top seen from above."""
+    return TOP(co.x + L.WIDTH / 2, L.DEPTH - co.y)
+
+
+def swatch(where):
+    x, y = where
+    return lambda co: (x / L.ATLAS, 1 - y / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+def paint(obj, mat, uv_of, keep):
+    """Gives the faces keep(centre, normal, material name) accepts the material mat and the UVs uv_of(corner)."""
+    mesh = obj.data
+    names = [m.name for m in mesh.materials]
+    if mat.name not in names:
+        mesh.materials.append(mat)
+        names.append(mat.name)
+    index = names.index(mat.name)
+    # One layer, the one exported as TEXCOORD_0: a boolean's cutter can bring a second, and joins match them by name.
+    while len(mesh.uv_layers) > 1:
+        mesh.uv_layers.remove(mesh.uv_layers[1])
+    uv = mesh.uv_layers[0] if mesh.uv_layers else mesh.uv_layers.new(name="UVMap")
+    uv.name = "UVMap"
+    for p in mesh.polygons:
+        if keep(p.center, p.normal, names[p.material_index]):
+            p.material_index = index
+            for li in p.loop_indices:
+                uv.data[li].uv = uv_of(mesh.vertices[mesh.loops[li].vertex_index].co)
+
+
+# ---- Geometry --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def solid(name, rings, mat):
+    """A solid through rings of 3D points (each the same count, in the same order), capped at both ends."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    verts = [[bm.verts.new(p) for p in ring] for ring in rings]
+    n = len(rings[0])
+    for a, b in zip(verts, verts[1:]):
+        for i in range(n):
+            j = (i + 1) % n
+            bm.faces.new([a[i], a[j], b[j], b[i]])
+    bm.faces.new(verts[0])
+    bm.faces.new(list(reversed(verts[-1])))
+    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
+    return new_object(name, bm, mat)
+
+
+def on_slope(name, outline, h0, h1, mat):
+    """A solid from an (x, s) outline on the deck, from h0 to h1 off it."""
+    return solid(name, [[SLOPE_FRAME @ Vector((x, s, h)) for x, s in outline] for h in (h0, h1)], mat)
+
+
+def rounded(cx, cz, w, h, r, segments=5):
+    """A rounded rectangle's outline in (x, z), w x h centred on (cx, cz), anticlockwise from its right side."""
+    points = []
+    for qx, qz, a0 in ((1, 1, 0), (-1, 1, 90), (-1, -1, 180), (1, -1, 270)):
+        ox, oz = cx + qx * (w / 2 - r), cz + qz * (h / 2 - r)
+        for k in range(segments + 1):
+            a = math.radians(a0 + 90 * k / segments)
+            points.append((ox + r * math.cos(a), oz + r * math.sin(a)))
+    return points
+
+
+def curved(name, w, h, bulge, uv, mat, nu=16, nv=12, keep=None):
+    """A screen facing the viewer (-y), w x h about its origin, its middle bulging bulge towards the viewer; uv(a, b)
+    gives the UV of the point a across from its left and b down from its top (both 0 to 1). keep(i, j), if given,
+    says which of its nu x nv cells to make (a part of the screen)."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    layer = bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
+    grid = [[bm.verts.new((w * (i / nu - 0.5), -bulge * (1 - (2 * i / nu - 1) ** 2) * (1 - (2 * j / nv - 1) ** 2),
+                           h * (0.5 - j / nv))) for i in range(nu + 1)] for j in range(nv + 1)]
+    for j in range(nv):
+        for i in range(nu):
+            if keep is not None and not keep(i, j):
+                continue
+            corners = ((i, j), (i, j + 1), (i + 1, j + 1), (i + 1, j))       # wound to face -y
+            face = bm.faces.new([grid[b][a] for a, b in corners])
+            face.smooth = True
+            for loop, (a, b) in zip(face.loops, corners):
+                loop[layer].uv = uv(a / nu, b / nv)

+    return new_object(name, bm, mat)
+
+
+def computer(m):
+    """The Amiga 500: the body cut for its wells, grooves, fins and drive, its top printed."""
+    body = prism_x("a500", L.profile(), -L.WIDTH / 2, L.WIDTH / 2, m["case"])
+    bevel(body, 1.6, segments=2)
+    boolean(body, join([on_slope("well", outline, -L.WELL, 12.0, m["dark"]) for outline in L.wells()], "wells"))
+    g = L.GROOVES
+    boolean(body, join([box("groove", g["x"][0], g["x"][1], y - g["width"] / 2, y + g["width"] / 2,

+"""The Amiga 500 and its Commodore 1084S monitor: the measurements shared by amiga_print.py (which draws their printing)
+and amiga.py (which builds them). Plain Python: Blender's Python imports it too.
+
+Millimetres. The computer: x from its middle (left to right), y back from its front edge, z up from the table. It's
+474 x 330 x 62 mm: a wedge whose keyboard deck rises from a low front edge to a step, behind which the raised back
+(the AMIGA lettering, nine vent grooves) rounds over into the comb of fins along its back edge, with the floppy drive
+in its right end. The monitor stands behind it, its front MONITOR["at"]: 357 x 330 mm, its hood shortened from the
+real 378 mm to 302 (the launcher fits a card's largest side, so the set's depth would draw it smaller than the other
+cards). The rest was measured from photographs on Wikimedia Commons (front views of the set, a top view, views of each
+end and of the back, and a 1084S from the side), scaled by the computer's width.
+
+The keyboard is the UK one. Its keys are laid out in units of U from the main block's left edge (KEYS_X0) and in rows
+from the front (row 5, the space bar's) to the back (row 1, the digits'), with the function keys behind them as row 0.
+The deck is a plane at SLOPE: a key stands on it in the slope's frame (x across, s up the slope from the deck's front
+edge, h off it), and deck_point() maps a point of that frame to the model's (y, z).
+
+Two textures. `print` (ATLAS square, PRINT_REGIONS): `top` (the computer's top seen from above: the key tops and their
+legends, the badge and lights, the AMIGA lettering; planar-mapped onto every face facing up) and `badge` (the
+monitor's), and swatches for plain parts. `media` (MEDIA_REGIONS): `kickstart` (the glass at rest: Kickstart 1.3's
+hand holding a disk) and `title` (the game's title screen), each the glass's whole width and height with the raster
+in its middle, drawn at the Amiga's 320 x 256 pixels; `disk_top` and `disk_bottom` (the floppy's two sides, as seen
+looking at each, its shutter to the left); and swatches. A region is (x, y, width, height) in pixels.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+ATLAS = 1024
+
+# -- The computer ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+WIDTH, DEPTH = 474.0, 330.0
+DECK = ((6.0, 23.0), (179.0, 39.0))     # the keyboard deck's front and back edges, (y, z)
+SLOPE = math.atan2(DECK[1][1] - DECK[0][1], DECK[1][0] - DECK[0][0])
+TOP_Z = 61.5                            # the raised back's top
+STEP_Y = 186.0                          # where the step up from the deck meets it
+FINS = dict(y=300.0, z=44.0)            # the top rounds over from y to the back edge, down to z there
+
+
+def profile():
+    """The computer's side outline, (y, z), anticlockwise seen from its right end."""
+    fy, fz = FINS["y"], FINS["z"]
+    back = [(fy + (DEPTH - fy) * math.sin(math.radians(a)), fz + (TOP_Z - fz) * math.cos(math.radians(a)))
+            for a in range(90, -1, -10)]
+    front = [(6.0 - 6.0 * math.sin(math.radians(a)), 17.0 + 6.0 * math.cos(math.radians(a))) for a in range(0, 91, 15)]
+    return ([(2.5, 0.0), (DEPTH - 2.5, 0.0), (DEPTH, 2.5)] + back + [(STEP_Y, TOP_Z), DECK[1], DECK[0]]

+
+def deck_point(s, h):
+    """The model's (y, z) of the point s up the deck's slope from its front edge and h off it."""
+    c, k = math.cos(SLOPE), math.sin(SLOPE)

+swatches small parts take their colour from. amiga_media.png: the two screens, each the glass's whole width and
+height, a dark border round the lit raster, drawn at the Amiga's 320 x 256 pixels: Kickstart 1.3's hand holding a

+def top_point(x, y):

+def key_top(reg, key):
+    """A key's top: its colour, a slightly lighter middle, and its legend at the top left (arrows and symbols in the
+    middle), the shifted character above the other."""
+    name, xu, row, wu, colour, legend = key[:6]
+    rows = key[6] if len(key) > 6 else 1
+    x0, s0, x1, s1 = L.key_rect(xu, row, wu, rows)
+    inset = L.KEY_INSET + 0.5
+    (ya, _), (yb, _) = L.deck_point(s0 + inset, L.KEY_HEIGHT), L.deck_point(s1 - inset, L.KEY_HEIGHT)
+    (rx0, ry0), (rx1, ry1) = top_point(x0 + inset, yb), top_point(x1 - inset, ya)
+    fill = rgb(L.COLOURS["top_light" if colour == "light" else "top_dark"])
+    reg.rect_(rx0 - 0.6, ry0 - 0.6, rx1 + 0.6, ry1 + 0.6, fill)
+    reg.rect_(rx0 + 1.2, ry0 + 1.2, rx1 - 1.2, ry1 - 1.2, shade(fill, 0.05), r=1.5)
+    if not legend:
+        return
+    if name in ("lamiga", "ramiga"):
+        reg.text("A", "timesbi.ttf", 5.0, rx0 + 2.2, ry0 + 3.4, LEGEND, anchor="lm")
+        return
+    lines = legend.split("\n")
+    symbol = len(lines) == 1 and len(legend) == 1 and not legend.isalnum()
+    if symbol or name.startswith("np") and len(lines[0]) == 1 and len(lines) == 1:
+        font = "seguisym.ttf" if not legend.isascii() else "arial.ttf"
+        reg.text(legend, font, 4.2 if not legend.isascii() else 3.4, (rx0 + rx1) / 2, (ry0 + ry1) / 2, LEGEND)
+        return
+    size = 2.4 if len(lines[0]) > 2 or len(lines) > 1 and len(lines[1]) > 2 else 3.0
+    for k, line in enumerate(lines):
+        font = "seguisym.ttf" if not line.isascii() else "arial.ttf"

+            reg.draw.text(reg.p(x + dx, ry + dy), ch, font=font, fill=colour, anchor="lm")

+"""The console theme's Apple II system model (godot/themes/console/models/systems/apple2.glb): an Apple IIe, two Disk
+II drives on its lid and a Monitor II on them, the IIe's banner on the screen while it looks for a disk.
+

+The computer is its side outline extruded across its width, standing on its dark base plate: the low front edge
+undercut beneath, the top sloping up to the flat top over its back two thirds; the keyboard's well and RESET's recess
+are cut into the slope, and the comb of vent slots into each side. Its 64 keys (the US layout) stand in the well,
+tapering to their printed tops, and the power light stands among them, lit. The drives are boxes, each with its front
+panel sunk into its front, the slot and the finger recess cut into it, the door's lever standing over the slot, and
+the vents in its sides. The monitor is its side outline extruded (its back sloping in at the top), the surround sunk
+into its front and the opening sloping in to the curved glass, a seam down its control strip. The printing is two
+textures drawn by apple2_print.py: the computer's top seen from above (planar-mapped onto every face facing up: the
+key tops and legends, the badge, the lid's seams), the drives' panels and the monitor's strip, with swatches; and the
+screens in green phosphor and the floppy.

+holding the floppy, drive 1's door (on its hinge) and its lit IN USE light, the three screens over the glass (Odyssey's
+title screen two and five eighths loaded, and whole), and Control and RESET. The floppy waits in drive 1 shrunk to
+nothing, the light and the screens are shrunk to nothing, so at rest the card is the set with the banner on the
+screen.
+
+The `focused` clip (8 s, looping) boots a game: the floppy slides into drive 1 and its door turns down over it; IN
+USE lights while the title screen arrives in hi-res's order, every eighth line first. Then Control and RESET go down
+together, the banner's back, the door turns up and the floppy comes out and goes.

+from the repo root:

+    python tools/console-models/apple2_print.py artifacts/apple2

+"""The Apple IIe, its two Disk II drives and its Monitor II: the measurements shared by apple2_print.py (which draws
+their printing) and apple2.py (which builds them). Plain Python: Blender's Python imports it too.
+
+Millimetres: x from the computer's middle (left to right), y back from its front edge, z up from the table. The IIe is
+392 x 448 x 108 mm: a wedge whose sloping top runs from its low front edge (undercut beneath) up to the flat top over
+its back two thirds, the keyboard in a well in the slope, RESET in a recess of its own at its right, the lid's front
+sloping down to the keyboard with the apple //e badge on it, and a comb of vent slots in each side. On its lid stand
+the two Disk II drives side by side, and on them the Monitor II, its depth cut from about 330 mm to 262 (the launcher
+fits a card's largest side, so the set's depth would draw it smaller than the other cards). Measured from photographs:
+the Bibliotheque nationale de France's set of an IIe and its drive (from above, in front, each side, the drive from
+above), a front view of the set on Wikimedia Commons, and close views of the US keyboard; scaled by the keys' 19.05 mm
+pitch.
+
+The keyboard is the US one. Its keys are laid out in units of U from the main block's left edge (KEYS_X0), in rows
+from the front (row 5, the space bar's) to the back (row 1, the digits'). The top slopes at SLOPE: a key stands on it
+in the slope's frame (x across, s up the slope from the front edge, h off it), and slope_point() maps a point of that
+frame to the model's (y, z).
+
+Two textures. `print` (ATLAS square, PRINT_REGIONS): `top` (the computer's top in front of the drives seen from
+above: the key tops and legends, the power light, the badge; planar-mapped onto every face facing up), `drive1` and
+`drive2` (the drives' front panels), `strip` (the monitor's control strip), and swatches. `media` (MEDIA_REGIONS):
+the screens, each the glass's whole width and height, green on black (`banner`, the screen at rest: Apple //e at its
+top; `pass2` and `pass5`, Odyssey's title screen part loaded, the hi-res lines in the order they arrive; `title`, the
+whole of it), the floppy's label side, and swatches. A region is (x, y, width, height) in pixels.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+ATLAS = 1024
+
+# -- The computer ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+WIDTH, DEPTH, HEIGHT = 392.0, 448.0, 108.0
+TIP = (0.0, 53.0)                     # the front edge's top
+FLAT_Y = 247.0                        # where the sloping top meets the flat top
+SLOPE = math.atan2(HEIGHT - TIP[1], FLAT_Y - TIP[0])
+UNDERCUT = (52.0, 4.0)                # the undercut runs back from under the front edge to here, (y, z)
+PLATE = 4.0                           # the dark base plate under it
+
+
+def profile():
+    """The computer's side outline, (y, z), anticlockwise seen from its right end."""
+    return [(UNDERCUT[0] + 4.0, 0.0), (DEPTH - 3.0, 0.0), (DEPTH, 3.0), (DEPTH, HEIGHT - 4.0), (DEPTH - 4.0, HEIGHT),
+            (FLAT_Y, HEIGHT), (TIP[0] + 2.0, TIP[1] + 0.45), (TIP[0], TIP[1] - 2.0), UNDERCUT]
+
+
+def slope_point(s, h):
+    """The model's (y, z) of the point s up the top's slope from the front edge and h off it."""
+    c, k = math.cos(SLOPE), math.sin(SLOPE)
+    return TIP[0] + s * c - h * k, TIP[1] + s * k + h * c

+
+SEAMS = dict(lid_front=139.0, lid_fold=243.0, lid_x=154.3)   # the lid's front edge and fold, along y; its sides, x
+BADGE = dict(x=(-141.5, -53.1), split=-79.8, y=(168.4, 192.0))  # apple and //e, side by side, on the lid's slope
+VENTS = dict(y=[252.0 + 10.6 * k for k in range(18)], width=4.2, z=(66.0, HEIGHT + 5.0), inset=12.0)
+
+# The keyboard: KEYS_X0 is the main block's left edge, U a key's pitch, GAP between two keys. A key stands from the
+# well's floor (WELL below the top) to its top, KEY_HEIGHT above it, tapering by KEY_INSET on every side.
+U, GAP = 19.05, 1.0
+KEYS_X0 = -140.0
+ROW_S = {5: 19.5, 4: 38.55, 3: 57.6, 2: 76.65, 1: 95.7}    # each row's front edge, up the slope
+WELL, KEY_HEIGHT, KEY_INSET = 4.0, 10.0, 2.4
+RESET = dict(x=(141.9, 158.3), s=(93.6, 108.9), well=(138.5, 161.7, 90.5, 112.0))
+
+

+
+
+def key_rect(xu, row, wu):

+
+
+def _row(names, x0, row, legends):
+    return [(n, x0 + i, row, 1.0, legend) for i, (n, legend) in enumerate(zip(names, legends))]
+
+

+KEYS = (
+    [("esc", 0.0, 1, 1.0, "Esc")]

+    + [("tab", 0.0, 2, 1.5, "Tab")]
+    + _row(list("qwertyuiop") + ["lbracket", "rbracket", "backslash"], 1.5, 2,
+           list("QWERTYUIOP") + ["{\n[", "}\n]", "|\n\\"])
+    + [("control", 0.0, 3, 1.75, "Control")]
+    + _row(list("asdfghjkl") + ["semicolon", "quote"], 1.75, 3, list("ASDFGHJKL") + [":\n;", '"\n\''])
+    + [("return", 12.75, 3, 1.75, "Return")]
+    + [("lshift", 0.0, 4, 2.25, "Shift")]
+    + _row(list("zxcvbnm") + ["comma", "period", "slash"], 2.25, 4, list("ZXCVBNM") + ["<\n,", ">\n.", "?\n/"])
+    + [("rshift", 12.25, 4, 2.25, "Shift")]
+    + [("caps", 0.0, 5, 1.25, "Caps\nLock"), ("grave", 1.25, 5, 1.0, "~\n`"), ("light", 2.25, 5, 1.0, ""),
+       ("open_apple", 3.25, 5, 1.0, "open"), ("space", 4.25, 5, 5.25, ""), ("solid_apple", 9.5, 5, 1.0, "solid")]
+    + _row(["left", "right", "down", "up"], 10.5, 5, ["←", "→", "↓", "↑"])
+)
+
+
+def well():
+    """The keyboard's well, an (x, s) outline."""
+    m = 1.6
+    s5, s1 = ROW_S[5] - m, ROW_S[1] + U + m
+    return [(kx(0) - m, s5), (kx(14.5) + m, s5), (kx(14.5) + m, s1), (kx(0) - m, s1)]
+
+
+# -- The Disk II drives ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+DRIVE = dict(size=(155.0, 222.0, 87.0), at=(-102.5, 102.5), front=244.0,
+             panel=(147.0, 79.0, 1.5),       # the front panel: w, h (centred), how far it's sunk into the front
+             slot=dict(z=40.0, height=3.2, x=(-64.0, 64.0), depth=150.0),  # z from the panel's bottom
+             door=dict(x=(-17.5, 17.5), z=(42.0, 66.0), thickness=4.5),   # the lever over the slot, open (up)
+             recess=dict(x=(-16.5, 16.5), z=(12.0, 37.0), depth=6.0),     # the finger recess under the slot
+             light=(-43.0, 14.5, 1.6),       # IN USE's light: its x, z from the panel's bottom, radius
+             vents=dict(y=[150.0 + 6.5 * k for k in range(9)], width=2.6, z=(55.0, 92.0)))
+PANEL_Z = HEIGHT + (DRIVE["size"][2] - DRIVE["panel"][1]) / 2   # the panels' bottom edge
+
+# -- The monitor -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+MONITOR = dict(
+    at=(0.0, 238.0),                 # its front's middle, in the computer's (x, y), standing on the drives
+    width=396.0,
+    profile=[(0.0, 0.0), (262.0, 0.0), (262.0, 236.0), (230.0, 292.0), (0.0, 292.0)],   # (y back, z)
+    strip=39.0,                      # the control strip down its right side, its width
+    bezel=dict(x=(-178.0, 144.0), z=(20.0, 256.0), depth=3.0),   # the screen's surround, sunk into the front
+    opening=dict(x=-17.0, z=138.0, outer=(300.0, 214.0, 14.0), inner=(268.0, 196.0, 10.0), depth=24.0),
+    glass=dict(size=(264.0, 192.0), bulge=8.0),
+)
+
+# -- The floppy ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+DISK = dict(size=133.0, thickness=1.6)                # a 5.25-inch floppy in its jacket
+SEAT = (DRIVE["at"][0], DRIVE["front"] + 8.0 + DISK["size"] / 2, PANEL_Z + DRIVE["slot"]["z"])   # its middle, in
+
+# -- The atlases -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+COLOURS = dict(case="#E3DCC4", keys="#A39E8F", bezel="#C5BCA6", dark="#2A2826", top_keys="#AEA99A",
+               drive="#29292B", plate="#5B544A")
+
+PRINT_REGIONS = dict(top=(0, 0, 1024, 653), drive1=(0, 661, 400, 225), drive2=(408, 661, 400, 225),
+                     strip=(816, 661, 80, 363))
+PRINT_SWATCHES = dict(bezel=(920, 680), dark=(952, 680), lit=(984, 680), plate=(920, 712), green=(952, 712),
+                      drive=(984, 712))
+
+SCREEN_PX = (504, 380)       # a screen's region, the glass's proportions
+RASTER = (448, 336)          # the lit picture in its middle, 4:3; the Apple's 280 x 192 drawn into it
+MEDIA_REGIONS = dict(banner=(0, 0) + SCREEN_PX, pass2=(512, 0) + SCREEN_PX, pass5=(0, 388) + SCREEN_PX,
+                     title=(512, 388) + SCREEN_PX, disk=(0, 776, 240, 240))
+MEDIA_SWATCHES = dict(black=(272, 800), jacket=(304, 800))
+
+# -- The focused clip ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+FPS = 30
+LENGTH = 240                 # 8 s

+"""The Apple IIe's, its Disk II drives' and its Monitor II's printing, for the console theme's Apple II model
+(tools/console-models/apple2.py).
+
+Draws its two atlases, their regions as apple2_layout.py places them. apple2_print.png: the computer's top in front of
+the drives, seen from above, in millimetres as the model's planar UVs map it (each key's top with its legend, the
+power light lit in the bottom row, the lid's seams and the apple //e badge), the two drives' front panels (DRIVE 1 and
+DRIVE 2, the IN USE lights off, disk II and the rainbow apple), the monitor's control strip (its power light lit, the
+switch, the badge), and the swatches small parts take their colour from. apple2_media.png: the screens, each the
+glass's whole width and height, the Apple's 280 x 192 pixels in green phosphor round a dark border (the banner the
+IIe shows looking for a disk; the title screen of a made-up game, Odyssey, two passes into loading, the hi-res lines
+arriving every eighth line at a time, and whole), and the floppy's label side. Run it with the system Python (Pillow):
+
+    python tools/console-models/apple2_print.py <out folder>
+
+It writes apple2_print.png and apple2_media.png there.
+"""
+
+import os
+import sys
+
+from PIL import Image, ImageChops, ImageDraw, ImageFilter, ImageFont
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import apple2_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+from psp_print import ship  # noqa: E402
+from retro_pc_print import rgb, shade  # noqa: E402
+from windows_pc_print import FONTS, Region  # noqa: E402
+
+CASE = rgb(L.COLOURS["case"])
+LEGEND = (58, 56, 52)
+RAINBOW = [(97, 187, 70), (253, 184, 39), (245, 130, 31), (224, 58, 62), (150, 61, 151), (0, 157, 220)]
+TOP_DEPTH = 250.0            # the top region's depth: the top in front of the drives
+PHOSPHOR, DARK_GLASS = (88, 255, 120), (8, 20, 12)
+
+
+def top_point(x, y):
+    """A point of the computer's top (x from its middle, y back from its front) in the top region's millimetres."""
+    return x + L.WIDTH / 2, TOP_DEPTH - y
+
+
+def slope_top(points, h):
+    """An (x, s) outline on the slope, raised h off it, in the top region's millimetres."""
+    return [top_point(x, L.slope_point(s, h)[0]) for x, s in points]
+
+
+# ---- The apple ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def apple(reg, cx, cy, h, fill=None, outline=None, width=0.3, rainbow=False):
+    """Apple's apple, h tall, its middle at (cx, cy): the body with its bite and the leaf; striped like the rainbow
+    logo, filled, or outlined."""
+    mask = Image.new("L", reg.img.size, 0)
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(mask)
+    w = h * 0.94
+    d.ellipse(reg.box(cx - w / 2, cy - h * 0.3, cx + w * 0.04, cy + h / 2), fill=255)
+    d.ellipse(reg.box(cx - w * 0.04, cy - h * 0.3, cx + w / 2, cy + h / 2), fill=255)
+    d.ellipse(reg.box(cx - w * 0.13, cy + h * 0.41, cx + w * 0.13, cy + h * 0.56), fill=0)    # the dip at its foot
+    d.ellipse(reg.box(cx + w * 0.3, cy - h * 0.1, cx + w * 0.68, cy + h * 0.28), fill=0)      # the bite
+    d.ellipse(reg.box(cx - w * 0.2, cy - h * 0.38, cx + w * 0.12, cy - h * 0.2), fill=0)      # the dip at its top
+    d.polygon([reg.p(cx + w * 0.02, cy - h * 0.34), reg.p(cx + w * 0.28, cy - h * 0.62),
+               reg.p(cx + w * 0.06, cy - h * 0.5)], fill=255)                                  # the leaf
+    if rainbow:
+        bands = Image.new("RGBA", reg.img.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
+        db = ImageDraw.Draw(bands)
+        top, bottom = cy - h * 0.62, cy + h / 2
+        for k, colour in enumerate(RAINBOW):
+            y0 = top + (bottom - top) * (0.0 if k == 0 else 0.33 + (k - 1) * 0.134)
+            y1 = top + (bottom - top) * (0.33 + k * 0.134)
+            db.rectangle(reg.box(cx - w, y0, cx + w, y1), fill=colour + (255,))
+        reg.img.paste(bands, (0, 0), mask)
+    elif fill is not None:
+        reg.img.paste(fill, (0, 0), mask)
+    if outline is not None:
+        edge = mask.filter(ImageFilter.FIND_EDGES).point(lambda v: 255 if v > 60 else 0)
+        edge = edge.filter(ImageFilter.MaxFilter(max(1, round(width * reg.sx)) | 1))
+        reg.img.paste(outline, (0, 0), edge)
+
+
+# ---- The computer's top ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def key_top(reg, name, xu, row, wu, legend):
+    x0, s0, x1, s1 = L.key_rect(xu, row, wu)
+    outline = [(x0, s0), (x1, s0), (x1, s1), (x0, s1)]
+    top = slope_top([(x0 + L.KEY_INSET, s0 + L.KEY_INSET), (x1 - L.KEY_INSET, s1 - L.KEY_INSET)], L.KEY_HEIGHT)
+    (ax, ay), (bx, by) = top
+    fill = rgb(L.COLOURS["top_keys"])
+    if name == "light":                                    # a pale window, the green light glowing in it
+        top = slope_top([(x0 + 1.0, s0 + 1.0), (x1 - 1.0, s1 - 1.0)], L.KEY_HEIGHT - 3.0)
+        (ax, ay), (bx, by) = top
+        reg.rect_(ax - 0.6, by - 0.6, bx + 0.6, ay + 0.6, (226, 224, 212))
+        glow = reg.layer()
+        cx, cy = (ax + bx) / 2, (ay + by) / 2
+        ImageDraw.Draw(glow).rounded_rectangle(reg.box(cx - 5.5, cy - 3.5, cx + 5.5, cy + 3.5), radius=2 * reg.sx,
+                                               fill=(110, 255, 90, 170))
+        reg.over(glow.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1.6 * reg.sx)))
+        reg.rect_(cx - 3.2, cy - 1.4, cx + 3.2, cy + 1.4, (150, 255, 120), r=0.8)
+        return
+    reg.rect_(ax - 0.7, by - 0.7, bx + 0.7, ay + 0.7, fill)
+    reg.rect_(ax + 1.0, by + 1.0, bx - 1.0, ay - 1.0, shade(fill, 0.05), r=1.4)
+    if not legend:
+        return
+    if legend in ("open", "solid"):
+        apple(reg, ax + 3.6, by + 3.6, 3.8, fill=LEGEND if legend == "solid" else None,
+              outline=LEGEND if legend == "open" else None, width=0.35)
+        return
+    lines = legend.split("\n")
+    if len(lines) == 1 and len(legend) == 1 and not legend.isalnum():
+        reg.text(legend, "seguisym.ttf", 4.0, (ax + bx) / 2, (ay + by) / 2, LEGEND)
+        return
+    if len(lines) == 1 and len(legend) == 1:
+        reg.text(legend, "arial.ttf", 3.4, ax + 2.6, by + 3.2, LEGEND)
+        return
+    size = 2.3 if max(len(line) for line in lines) > 2 else 3.0
+    for k, line in enumerate(lines):
+        reg.text(line, "arial.ttf", size, ax + 1.8, by + 2.6 + k * (size + 1.0), LEGEND, anchor="lm")
+
+
+def badge(reg):
+    (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = top_point(L.BADGE["x"][0], L.BADGE["y"][1]), top_point(L.BADGE["x"][1], L.BADGE["y"][0])
+    split = top_point(L.BADGE["split"], 0.0)[0]
+    plate = (78, 74, 70)
+    reg.rect_(x0, y0, split - 1.2, y1, plate, r=1.4)
+    reg.rect_(split + 1.2, y0, x1, y1, plate, r=1.4)
+    h = y1 - y0
+    apple(reg, x0 + 0.36 * h, (y0 + y1) / 2 + 0.4, h * 0.66, rainbow=True)
+    layer = reg.layer()
+    f = ImageFont.truetype(FONTS + "arialbd.ttf", max(1, round(h * 0.62 * reg.sx)))
+    ImageDraw.Draw(layer).text(reg.p(x0 + 0.72 * h, (y0 + y1) / 2 + 0.6), "apple", font=f, fill=(226, 224, 218, 255),
+                               anchor="lm")
+    ImageDraw.Draw(layer).text(reg.p((split + x1) / 2 + 0.3, (y0 + y1) / 2 + 0.6), "//e", font=f,
+                               fill=(226, 224, 218, 255), anchor="mm")
+    reg.over(layer.transform(layer.size, Image.AFFINE, (1, 0.22, -0.22 * reg.p(0, (y0 + y1) / 2)[1], 0, 1, 0)))
+
+
+def top():
+    reg = Region(L.PRINT_REGIONS["top"], L.WIDTH, TOP_DEPTH, CASE)
+    seam = shade(CASE, -0.32)
+    lx = L.SEAMS["lid_x"]
+    (sx0, sy), (sx1, _) = top_point(-lx, L.SEAMS["lid_front"]), top_point(lx, L.SEAMS["lid_front"])
+    reg.line([(sx0, sy), (sx1, sy)], seam, 0.5)
+    for x in (-lx, lx):
+        a, b = top_point(x, L.SEAMS["lid_front"]), top_point(x, TOP_DEPTH)
+        reg.line([a, b], seam, 0.5)
+    fold = top_point(0.0, L.SEAMS["lid_fold"])[1]
+    reg.line([(sx0, fold), (sx1, fold)], shade(CASE, -0.08), 0.6)
+    badge(reg)
+    for name, xu, row, wu, legend in L.KEYS:
+        key_top(reg, name, xu, row, wu, legend)
+    x0, x1 = L.RESET["x"]
+    s0, s1 = L.RESET["s"]
+    (ax, ay), (bx, by) = slope_top([(x0 + 1.6, s0 + 1.6), (x1 - 1.6, s1 - 1.6)], 6.0)
+    fill = rgb(L.COLOURS["top_keys"])
+    reg.rect_(ax - 0.7, by - 0.7, bx + 0.7, ay + 0.7, fill)
+    reg.rect_(ax + 0.8, by + 0.8, bx - 0.8, ay - 0.8, shade(fill, 0.05), r=1.0)
+    reg.text("Reset", "arial.ttf", 2.2, (ax + bx) / 2, (ay + by) / 2, LEGEND)
+    return reg
+
+
+# ---- The drives and the monitor's strip --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def drive_panel(n):
+    w, h, _ = L.DRIVE["panel"]
+    base = rgb(L.COLOURS["drive"])
+    reg = Region(L.PRINT_REGIONS[f"drive{n}"], w, h, base)

+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(grain)
+    for k in range(2600):                                   # the panel's fine texture
+        x, y = (k * 7919) % (reg.img.size[0]), (k * 104729 // 3) % (reg.img.size[1])
+        d.point((x, y), fill=(255, 255, 255, 10 + k % 14))
+    reg.over(grain)
+
+    def at(x, z):
+        return x + w / 2, h - z
+    reg.text("DRIVE", "arial.ttf", 3.0, *at(46.0, 52.5), (214, 214, 212), anchor="rm")
+    reg.text(str(n), "arial.ttf", 6.0, *at(52.5, 53.2), (214, 214, 212))
+    lx, lz, r = L.DRIVE["light"]
+    reg.text("IN USE", "arial.ttf", 2.6, *at(lx - 4.6, lz), (214, 214, 212), anchor="rm")
+    ax, ay = at(lx - 3.6, lz)
+    reg.poly([(ax, ay - 1.2), (ax + 2.0, ay), (ax, ay + 1.2)], (214, 214, 212))
+    reg.circle(*at(lx, lz), r + 0.5, (16, 16, 18))

+The IIGS is its plinth (the lip sloping along its front) and its main box, grooved across its top and along its sides,
+the seam between its lid and its base rising along its sides. The monitor's deep front frame stands on it, the screen's
+opening sloping in to the curved glass, its housing behind, grooved along its sides and top, three knobs in its right
+side. The drive is a low box, its slot cut high in its front, its top grooved. The keyboard is a wedge, its keys
+standing on it, tapering to their printed tops, a blank column between the main block and the keypad, the raised
+strip behind with the power key; the mouse a box domed towards its back. The printing is two textures drawn by
+apple2gs_print.py: the keyboard's top, the IIGS's, the monitor's and the drive's fronts, the mouse's top and swatches;
+and the screens and the disk.
+
+A node tree: a root (the turn to a three-quarter view, TILT_YAW and TILT_PITCH: the right side towards the viewer, the

+screens over the glass (GS/OS starting, and the title screen and a moment of play of a made-up game, Odyssey), shrunk
+to nothing, and RETURN.
+
+The `focused` clip (8 s, looping) boots a game: the disk slides into the drive and its light flickers; GS/OS starts
+and Odyssey's title comes up; RETURN is pressed and the game starts; then the eject button goes in, the disk pops out
+and goes, and Check startup device! is back.
+

+repo root:
+
+    python tools/console-models/apple2gs_print.py artifacts/apple2gs
