+"""The console theme's Acorn Electron system model (godot/themes/console/models/systems/electron.glb): an Acorn
+Electron with a Plus 1 on its back, in front of the portable television the ZX Spectrum's card has.
+
+Built in Blender (electron_layout.py has the measurements, taken from photographs). The computer is its side outline (a
+wedge, its top sloping up to the back) extruded across its width, the keys' opening cut into its top; its 56 keys stand
+in the opening in the slope's frame, each tapering to its printed top. The Plus 1 is a box on its back, its two slots
+cut into its top, the second under its cover. Behind it stands zx_spectrum.py's television. The printing is one texture
+(electron_print.py's), planar-mapped from above onto every face facing up.
+
+A node tree: a root (the turn to a three-quarter view, TILT_YAW and TILT_PITCH: the right end towards the viewer, the
+top tipped up; then the model spec's fit: standing on y = 0, centred, the largest side 1 m) holding the set; the set
+holding the cartridge (waiting over the first slot, shrunk to nothing), the first slot's cover (on its hinge), the
+television's four screens (those not shown behind the glass) and the keys the clip presses.
+
+The `focused` clip (8 s, looping): the cartridge appears over the Plus 1, turns to show its label and drops into the
+first slot, the cover swinging down out of its way; CTRL and BREAK start it, its title comes up; SPACE, and the game's
+played on Z, X and RETURN; BREAK brings the start-up screen back and the cartridge rises out and goes.
+
+Four materials (case, tv, dark, glass) and one 1024² texture, within the system model budget. Run from the repo root:
+
+    python tools/console-models/electron_print.py artifacts/electron
+    blender -b --factory-startup --python tools/console-models/electron.py -- artifacts/electron godot/themes/console/models/systems/electron.glb
+"""
+
+import math
+import os
+import sys
+
+import bpy
+from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import electron_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+import zx_spectrum_layout as SL  # noqa: E402
+from amiga import curved, paint, solid  # noqa: E402
+from clip import HIDDEN, Pose, back_out, ease_in, ease_out, key, phase, smooth  # noqa: E402
+from mega_drive_cartridge import (bevel, boolean, box, export, join, material, prism_x,  # noqa: E402
+                                  triangles)
+from zx_spectrum import television  # noqa: E402
+
+TILT_YAW = -24.0     # degrees about the vertical: the right end comes towards the viewer
+TILT_PITCH = 20.0    # degrees about the horizontal: the top tips up towards the viewer
+ROUGHNESS = dict(case=0.5, tv=0.45, dark=0.7, glass=0.35)
+MOVING = {"CTRL": "ctrl", "BREAK": "break", "RETURN": "return", "Z": "z", "X": "x", " ": "space"}
+TOTAL_DEPTH = L.PLUS1["y"][1]
+
+
+def atlas_uv(region, w, h):
+    rx, ry, rw, rh = region
+    return lambda a, b: ((rx + a / w * rw) / L.ATLAS, 1 - (ry + b / h * rh) / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+def swatch(name):
+    x, y = L.SWATCHES[name]
+    return lambda co: (x / L.ATLAS, 1 - y / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+def colour(obj, mat, name):
+    paint(obj, mat, swatch(name), lambda c, n, kind: True)
+    return obj
+
+
+TOP = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["top"], L.WIDTH, TOTAL_DEPTH)
+
+
+def top_uv(co):
+    return TOP(co.x + L.WIDTH / 2, TOTAL_DEPTH - co.y)
+
+
+def on_slope(name, outline, h0, h1, mat):
+    """A solid from an (x, s) outline in the slope's frame, from h0 to h1 off it."""
+    return solid(name, [[(x, *L.top_point(s, h)) for x, s in outline] for h in (h0, h1)], mat)
+
+
+# ---- The computer and the Plus 1 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def computer(m):
+    """The wedge, the keys' opening cut into its top, the Plus 1 on its back with its slots; printed from above."""
+    half = L.WIDTH / 2
+    body = prism_x("electron", L.profile(), -half, half, m["case"])
+    bevel(body, 2.4, segments=2, angle=40)
+    (ox0, ox1), (s0, s1), depth = L.OPENING["x"], L.OPENING["s"], L.OPENING["depth"]
+    boolean(body, on_slope("opening", [(ox0, s0), (ox1, s0), (ox1, s1), (ox0, s1)], -depth, 20.0, m["case"]))
+    (py0, py1), ph = L.PLUS1["y"], L.PLUS1["height"]
+    plus1 = box("plus1", -half, half, py0 + 0.5, py1, 0.0, ph, m["case"])
+    bevel(plus1, 2.4, segments=2, angle=40)
+    (cx0, cx1), sd = L.PLUS1["x"], L.PLUS1["depth"]
+    for sy0, sy1 in L.PLUS1["slots"]:
+        boolean(plus1, box("slot", cx0, cx1, sy0, sy1, ph - sd, ph + 5.0, m["case"]))
+    parts = [body, plus1]
+    for part in parts:
+        colour(part, m["case"], "case")
+        paint(part, m["case"], top_uv, lambda c, n, kind: n.z > 0.5)
+        paint(part, m["case"], swatch("dark"),
+              lambda c, n, kind: cx0 - 0.5 < c.x < cx1 + 0.5 and c.z < ph - 0.5 and c.y > py0
+              and any(a - 0.5 < c.y < b + 0.5 for a, b in L.PLUS1["slots"]))
+    sy0, sy1 = L.PLUS1["slots"][1]                              # the second slot's cover, shut
+    cover = box("cover", cx0 + 0.4, cx1 - 0.4, sy0 + 0.4, sy1 - 0.4, ph - 2.0, ph - 0.4, m["case"])
+    colour(cover, m["case"], "case")
+    paint(cover, m["case"], top_uv, lambda c, n, kind: n.z > 0.9)
+    return join(parts + [cover], "electron")
+
+
+def keys(m):
+    """The keys, each tapering from the opening's floor to its printed top in the slope's frame: those the clip presses
+    apart (each its foot's middle at its origin, with where it goes), the rest joined."""
+    fixed, moving = [], {}
+    inset, h1 = L.KEY["inset"], L.KEY["height"] - L.OPENING["depth"]
+    for legend, x0, x1, s in L.keys():
+        foot = [(x0 + 0.6, s - 9.0), (x1 - 0.6, s - 9.0), (x1 - 0.6, s + 9.0), (x0 + 0.6, s + 9.0)]
+        cap = [(x0 + inset, s - 9.5 + inset), (x1 - inset, s - 9.5 + inset), (x1 - inset, s + 9.5 - inset),
+               (x0 + inset, s + 9.5 - inset)]
+        h0 = -L.OPENING["depth"]
+        part = solid("key", [[(x, *L.top_point(ss, h0)) for x, ss in foot],
+                             [(x, *L.top_point(ss, h1)) for x, ss in cap]], m["case"])
+        colour(part, m["case"], "key")
+        paint(part, m["case"], top_uv, lambda c, n, kind: n.z > 0.9)
+        name = MOVING.get(legend)
+        if name and name not in moving:
+            y, z = L.top_point(s, h0)
+            middle = Vector(((x0 + x1) / 2, y, z))
+            part.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(-middle))
+            moving[name] = (part, middle)
+        else:
+            fixed.append(part)
+    return join(fixed, "keys"), moving
+
+
+def cover(m):
+    """The first slot's cover, its origin on its hinge along the slot's back edge, shut."""
+    (cx0, cx1), ph = L.PLUS1["x"], L.PLUS1["height"]
+    sy0, sy1 = L.PLUS1["slots"][0]
+    part = box("cover_1", cx0 + 0.4, cx1 - 0.4, sy0 + 0.4, sy1 - 0.4, ph - 2.0, ph - 0.4, m["case"])
+    colour(part, m["case"], "case")
+    paint(part, m["case"], top_uv, lambda c, n, kind: n.z > 0.9)
+    hinge = Vector((0.0, sy1 - 0.4, ph - 1.2))
+    part.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(-hinge))
+    return part, hinge
+
+
+def cartridge(m):
+    """The cartridge, its foot's middle at its origin, its label facing -y."""
+    w, t, h = L.CART["size"]
+    part = box("cartridge", -w / 2, w / 2, -t / 2, t / 2, 0.0, h, m["case"])
+    bevel(part, 1.6, segments=2)
+    colour(part, m["case"], "cart")
+    lw, lh = L.CART["label"]
+    face = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["label"], lw, lh)
+    z1 = h - 6.0
+    paint(part, m["case"], lambda co: face(co.x + lw / 2, z1 - co.z),
+          lambda c, n, kind: n.y < -0.9 and abs(c.x) < lw / 2 and z1 - lh < c.z < z1)
+    return part
+
+
+def screens(m):
+    """The television's four screens (boot, title, game_1, game_2), each the glass's whole area."""
+    gw, gh = SL.TV["glass"]["size"]
+    out = {}
+    for name in ("boot", "title", "game_1", "game_2"):
+        out[name] = curved(name, gw, gh, SL.TV["glass"]["bulge"], atlas_uv(L.REGIONS[name], 1.0, 1.0), m["glass"])
+    return out
+
+
+# ---- The focused clip ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+BEHIND = 3.0              # how far back a screen that isn't shown waits: behind the glass
+
+
+def tap(f, f0, hold=2):
+    return smooth(phase(f, f0, f0 + 3)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, f0 + 3 + hold, f0 + 7 + hold)))
+
+
+def shown(f):
+    if f < 52 or f >= 188:
+        return "boot"
+    if f < 96:
+        return "title"
+    return "game_1" if ((f - 96) // 8) % 2 == 0 else "game_2"
+
+
+def timeline(f):
+    above = L.CART["above"]
+    if f < 8 or f >= 214:
+        cart = Pose(z=above, scale=HIDDEN)
+    elif f < 16:
+        cart = Pose(z=above, scale=max(HIDDEN, back_out(phase(f, 8, 15))))
+    elif f < 30:
+        cart = Pose(z=above, spin=360.0 * smooth(phase(f, 16, 30)))
+    elif f < 42:
+        cart = Pose(z=above * (1 - ease_in(phase(f, 30, 42))))
+    elif f < 194:
+        cart = Pose(z=-1.6 * math.sin(math.pi * phase(f, 42, 48)))
+    elif f < 206:
+        cart = Pose(z=above * ease_out(phase(f, 194, 206)))
+    else:
+        cart = Pose(z=above, scale=max(HIDDEN, 1 - ease_in(phase(f, 206, 214))))
+    swing = 92.0 * smooth(phase(f, 36, 41)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 202, 208)))
+    poses = {"cartridge": cart, "cover": Pose(pitch=-swing)}
+    for name in ("boot", "title", "game_1", "game_2"):
+        poses[name] = Pose() if name == shown(f) else Pose(y=BEHIND)
+    press = -2.4
+    poses["ctrl"] = Pose(z=press * smooth(phase(f, 44, 47)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 52, 55))))
+    poses["break"] = Pose(z=press * max(tap(f, 47), tap(f, 184)))
+    poses["space"] = Pose(z=press * tap(f, 92))
+    poses["z"] = Pose(z=press * max(tap(f, f0) for f0 in (104, 128, 152)))
+    poses["x"] = Pose(z=press * max(tap(f, f0) for f0 in (116, 140, 164)))
+    poses["return"] = Pose(z=press * max(tap(f, f0) for f0 in (110, 134, 160)))
+    return poses
+
+
+# ---- Main ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def main():
+    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
+    images, out = os.path.abspath(args[0]), os.path.abspath(args[1])
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
+    scene = bpy.context.scene
+    scene.render.fps = L.FPS
+    atlas = bpy.data.images.load(os.path.join(images, "electron_print.png"))
+    m = {"case": material("case", L.COLOURS["print"], ROUGHNESS["case"], atlas),
+         "tv": material("tv", SL.COLOURS["tv"], ROUGHNESS["tv"]),
+         "dark": material("dark", L.COLOURS["dark"], ROUGHNESS["dark"]),
+         "glass": material("glass", L.COLOURS["print"], ROUGHNESS["glass"], atlas)}
+    m["print"] = m["case"]                                    # television() prints its front with the set's atlas
+
+    fixed_keys, moving_keys = keys(m)

+    shift = Matrix.Translation((L.TV_AT[0] - SL.TV["at"][0], L.TV_AT[1] - SL.TV["at"][1], 0.0))
+    for part in tv:
+        part.data.transform(shift)

+    for p in whole.data.polygons:
+        p.use_smooth = True
+    whole.data.set_sharp_from_angle(angle=math.radians(35))
+
+    root = bpy.data.objects.new("electron_root", None)
+    scene.collection.objects.link(root)
+    whole.parent = root
+    s = SL.TV["screen"]
+    glass_front = Vector((L.TV_AT[0] + s["x"], L.TV_AT[1] + s["depth"] - 0.4, s["z"]))
+    flap, hinge = cover(m)
+    (cx0, cx1) = L.PLUS1["x"]
+    sy0, sy1 = L.PLUS1["slots"][0]
+    seat = Vector(((cx0 + cx1) / 2, (sy0 + sy1) / 2, L.PLUS1["height"] - L.CART["seat"]))
+    parts = {"cartridge": (cartridge(m), seat), "cover": (flap, hinge)}
+    parts.update({name: (part, glass_front) for name, part in screens(m).items()})

+    points = [tilt @ v.co for v in whole.data.vertices]
+    lo = Vector([min(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    hi = Vector([max(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    size = hi - lo
+    root.matrix_world = Matrix.Scale(1 / max(size), 4) @ Matrix.Translation((-(lo.x + hi.x) / 2, -(lo.y + hi.y) / 2,
+                                                                             -lo.z)) @ tilt

+    key("focused", nodes, timeline, L.LENGTH)
+    meshes = [whole] + list(nodes.values())
+    print(f"Electron: {sum(triangles(o.data) for o in meshes)} triangles ({triangles(whole.data)} the set), "
+          f"{len({mat.name for o in meshes for mat in o.data.materials})} materials, "
+          f"size {size.x:.1f} x {size.y:.1f} x {size.z:.1f} mm tilted, before the fit")
+    export([root] + meshes, out, animations=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""The Acorn Electron card's measurements, shared by electron_print.py (which draws its printing and screens) and
+electron.py (which builds it). Plain Python: Blender's Python imports it too.
+
+The Acorn Electron (1983), 340 mm wide, 160 deep and 65 high (a retro computing database's figures), a Plus 1 on its
+back (340 x 90 x 50, as the period's pages give it) with a ROM cartridge going into its slot, in front of the portable
+television the ZX Spectrum's card has (zx_spectrum.py's, its front's middle at TV_AT). Millimetres: x from the
+computer's middle (left to right), y back from its front, z up from the table. The rest was measured from photographs of
+Electrons on Wikimedia Commons (from above with a Plus 1 on, from the front corners), scaled by its width and by its
+keys' 19.05 mm pitch.
+
+The computer: a wedge, its top sloping up from the front to the back; the keys (the UK layout) standing in the opening
+in its top, the dark band behind them (its grid of lines, acorn electron and the green acorn). The Plus 1: a box on its
+back, the two cartridge slots in its top's right half, each under a hinged cover.
+
+The keys are laid out in units of U from the back row's left edge (KEYS_X0), in rows from the back (the digits') to the
+front (the space bar's). The top is a plane at SLOPE: a key stands on it in the slope's frame (x across, s up the slope
+from its front edge, h off it), and top_point() maps a point of that frame to the model's (y, z).
+
+One texture (ATLAS square, REGIONS): `top` (the computer and the Plus 1 seen from above: the key tops and legends, the
+band; planar-mapped onto every face facing up), `label` (the cartridge's), the screens (`boot`, `title`, `game_1`,
+`game_2`), and swatches; the television's front drawn where zx_spectrum_layout.py's PRINT_REGIONS["tv"] puts it and its
+swatches where its PRINT_SWATCHES do, as television() maps them. A region is (x, y, width, height) in pixels.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+ATLAS = 1024
+U = 19.05
+
+WIDTH, DEPTH = 340.0, 160.0
+FRONT = (8.0, 26.0)              # the top's front edge (y, z)
+BACK = (154.0, 62.0)             # where the top meets the back's rounding
+SLOPE = math.atan2(BACK[1] - FRONT[1], BACK[0] - FRONT[0])
+OPENING = dict(x=(-160.0, 152.0), s=(6.0, 116.0), depth=5.0)     # the keys' opening in the top
+BAND = dict(s=(118.0, 148.0))    # the dark band behind the keys
+KEYS_X0, KEY_ROW1 = -146.0, 104.0   # the back row's left edge; its middle (s)
+KEY = dict(height=12.0, inset=2.6)  # a key's height off the opening's floor; how far its top is drawn in
+ROWS = [
+    (0.0, [("ESCAPE", 1.0)] + [(c, 1.0) for c in "1234567890=^\\"] + [("BREAK", 1.0)]),
+    (0.5, [("CAPS LK", 1.25)] + [(c, 1.0) for c in "QWERTYUIOP£_"] + [("COPY", 1.0)]),
+    (0.75, [("CTRL", 1.25)] + [(c, 1.0) for c in "ASDFGHJKL;:"] + [("RETURN", 1.75)]),
+    (0.9, [("SHIFT", 1.6)] + [(c, 1.0) for c in "ZXCVBNM,./"] + [("SHIFT", 1.25), ("DELETE", 1.0)]),
+    (3.0, [(" ", 7.5)]),
+]
+
+PLUS1 = dict(y=(160.0, 250.0), height=52.0, slots=[(176.0, 192.0), (212.0, 228.0)], x=(28.0, 152.0), depth=34.0)
+CART = dict(size=(104.0, 15.0, 78.0), seat=34.0, label=(80.0, 52.0), above=70.0)   # w, t, h; how deep it sits;
+                                                                                   # how far over it it appears
+TV_AT = (0.0, 262.0)             # the television's front's middle
+
+COLOURS = dict(case="#E4DCC6", key="#ECE6D4", band="#3B4038", dark="#0A0A0B", print="#FFFFFF")
+
+REGIONS = dict(top=(0, 0, 850, 625), label=(858, 0, 160, 104), boot=(828, 796, 192, 148), title=(632, 640, 192, 148),
+               game_1=(828, 640, 192, 148), game_2=(632, 796, 192, 148))
+SWATCHES = dict(case=(872, 140), key=(904, 140), band=(936, 140), dark=(968, 140), cart=(872, 172), lit=(904, 172))
+
+FPS = 30
+LENGTH = 240                 # 8 s
+
+
+def top_point(s, h):
+    """The model's (y, z) of the point s up the top's slope from its front edge and h off it."""
+    c, k = math.cos(SLOPE), math.sin(SLOPE)
+    return FRONT[0] + s * c - h * k, FRONT[1] + s * k + h * c
+
+
+def profile():
+    """The computer's side outline, (y, z), round from its front's foot: the front, the slope, the back rounding over
+    and down, the underside."""
+    by, bz = BACK
+    back = [(by + (DEPTH - by) * math.sin(math.radians(a)), bz - 6.0 + 6.0 * math.cos(math.radians(a)))
+            for a in range(0, 91, 15)]
+    return [(2.0, 0.0), (DEPTH - 2.0, 0.0), (DEPTH, 2.0)] + list(reversed(back)) + [FRONT, (0.0, FRONT[1] - 4.0),
+                                                                                    (0.0, 2.0)]
+
+
+def keys():
+    """Every key: (legend, x0, x1, s), s its row's middle up the slope; the rows from the back to the front."""
+    out = []
+    for r, (offset, row) in enumerate(ROWS):
+        x = KEYS_X0 + offset * U
+        s = KEY_ROW1 - r * U
+        for legend, width in row:
+            out.append((legend, x, x + width * U, s))
+            x += width * U
+    return out

+"""The Acorn Electron card's printing and screens (electron_print.png), for the console theme's model (electron.py).
+
+One image, laid out as electron_layout.REGIONS says: the computer and the Plus 1 from above (the key tops and legends,
+the dark band with its grid, acorn electron and the green acorn, the Plus 1's slot covers), the cartridge's label (a
+made-up game, Odyssey), the screens (the Electron's start-up screen, then the game's title and two moments of its play
+in Mode 2's eight colours, drawn as the BBC Micro's are), the television's front (zx_spectrum_print.py's, where its
+layout puts it), and swatches. Run it with the system Python (Pillow):
+
+    python tools/console-models/electron_print.py <out folder>
+"""
+
+import os
+import sys
+
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import electron_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+import zx_spectrum_layout as SL  # noqa: E402
+from bbcmicro_print import game, mode7, title  # noqa: E402
+from psp_print import ship, space  # noqa: E402
+from retro_pc_print import rgb  # noqa: E402
+from windows_pc_print import FONTS, Region  # noqa: E402
+from zx_spectrum_print import tv_front  # noqa: E402
+
+CASE = rgb(L.COLOURS["case"])
+KEY = rgb(L.COLOURS["key"])
+BAND = rgb(L.COLOURS["band"])
+INK = (40, 40, 44)
+GREEN = (110, 200, 60)
+
+
+def top():
+    """The computer and the Plus 1 from above: x across (-170 at the left), y down from the Plus 1's back (250)."""
+    w, d = L.WIDTH, L.PLUS1["y"][1]
+    reg = Region(L.REGIONS["top"], w, d, CASE)
+
+    def at(x, y):
+        return x + w / 2, d - y
+
+    # The opening's floor and the band.
+    (ox0, ox1), (s0, s1) = L.OPENING["x"], L.OPENING["s"]
+    reg.rect_(*at(ox0, L.top_point(s1, 0.0)[0]), *at(ox1, L.top_point(s0, 0.0)[0]), (176, 168, 150))
+    (b0, b1) = L.BAND["s"]
+    y0, y1 = L.top_point(b0, 0.0)[0], L.top_point(b1, 0.0)[0]
+    reg.rect_(*at(-w / 2 + 6.0, y1), *at(w / 2 - 6.0, y0), BAND)
+    x = -w / 2 + 6.0
+    while x < w / 2 - 6.0:
+        reg.line([at(x, y0), at(x, y1)], (88, 96, 84), 0.25)
+        x += 4.0
+    yy = y0
+    while yy < y1:
+        reg.line([at(-w / 2 + 6.0, yy), at(w / 2 - 6.0, yy)], (88, 96, 84), 0.25)
+        yy += 4.0
+    my = (y0 + y1) / 2
+    reg.text("acorn", "arialbd.ttf", 7.0, *at(-140.0, my), (240, 240, 236), anchor="lm")
+    reg.draw.ellipse(reg.box(*at(-111.5, my + 4.6), *at(-104.5, my - 4.8)), fill=GREEN)
+    reg.text("electron", "arialbd.ttf", 7.0, *at(-102.0, my), (240, 240, 236), anchor="lm")
+    # The keys' tops.
+    for legend, kx0, kx1, s in L.keys():
+        ya, yb = L.top_point(s - 9.5 + L.KEY["inset"], L.KEY["height"] - L.OPENING["depth"])[0], \
+            L.top_point(s + 9.5 - L.KEY["inset"], L.KEY["height"] - L.OPENING["depth"])[0]
+        reg.rect_(*at(kx0 + L.KEY["inset"], yb), *at(kx1 - L.KEY["inset"], ya), KEY, r=1.2)
+        if legend.strip():
+            size = 4.4 if len(legend) <= 2 else 2.2
+            reg.text(legend, "arialbd.ttf" if len(legend) > 2 else "arial.ttf", size,
+                     *at((kx0 + kx1) / 2, (ya + yb) / 2), INK)
+    # The Plus 1's slot covers.
+    (cx0, cx1) = L.PLUS1["x"]
+    for (sy0, sy1) in L.PLUS1["slots"]:
+        reg.rect_(*at(cx0 - 3.0, sy1 + 3.0), *at(cx1 + 3.0, sy0 - 3.0), (200, 192, 172), r=2.0)
+        reg.rect_(*at(cx0, sy1), *at(cx1, sy0), (220, 212, 192), r=1.0)
+    reg.text("PLUS 1", "arialbd.ttf", 4.0, *at(-110.0, 205.0), (150, 142, 124))
+    return reg
+
+
+def label():
+    lw, lh = L.CART["label"]
+    reg = Region(L.REGIONS["label"], lw, lh, (20, 20, 24))
+    art = space((480, 312)).convert("RGB")
+    ship(ImageDraw.Draw(art), 150, 190, 3.0, "#FFFFFF", "#FFB23C")
+    x0, y0, x1, y1 = reg.box(0.0, 12.0, lw, lh)
+    reg.img.paste(art.resize((round(x1 - x0), round(y1 - y0)), Image.LANCZOS), (round(x0), round(y0)))
+    reg.rect_(0.0, 0.0, lw, 12.0, (16, 16, 18))
+    reg.text("ODYSSEY", "ariblk.ttf", 7.0, lw / 2, 6.0, (255, 214, 70))
+    return reg
+
+
+def boot():
+    return mode7([(0, 0, "Acorn Electron", "white", False), (2, 0, "BASIC", "white", False),
+                  (4, 0, ">_", "white", False)])
+
+
+def main(out):
+    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
+    image = Image.new("RGB", (L.ATLAS, L.ATLAS), CASE)
+    for reg in (top(), label(), tv_front()):
+        reg.paste(image)
+    for name, screen in (("boot", boot()), ("title", title()), ("game_1", game(0)), ("game_2", game(1))):
+        x, y, w, h = L.REGIONS[name]
+        image.paste(screen.resize((w, h), Image.LANCZOS), (x, y))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
+    for name, colour in (("black", rgb(SL.COLOURS["bezel"])), ("silver", rgb(SL.COLOURS["handle"])),
+                         ("red", (255, 40, 30))):
+        x, y = SL.PRINT_SWATCHES[name]
+        d.rectangle([x - 12, y - 12, x + 11, y + 11], fill=colour)
+    colours = dict(case=CASE, key=KEY, band=BAND, dark=rgb(L.COLOURS["dark"]), cart=(24, 24, 26), lit=(255, 60, 40))
+    for name, (x, y) in L.SWATCHES.items():
+        d.rectangle([x - 12, y - 12, x + 11, y + 11], fill=colours[name])
+    path = os.path.join(out, "electron_print.png")
+    image.save(path, optimize=True)
+    print(path)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main(sys.argv[1])

+"""The console theme's Famicom Disk System model (godot/themes/console/models/systems/fds.glb): a Famicom with its RAM
+adapter, sitting on its Disk System drive, a disk card going in.
+
+Built in Blender from the real machines' proportions (fds_layout.py has the measurements, taken from photographs). The
+drive is a rounded red box, the seam cut round it, the black panel, the slot's bay and the slot (deep enough for the
+whole card) cut into its front. The Famicom on it: the dark red base; the white shell, its side outline extruded
+across its width (the front slope, the front deck, the step, the back deck); the EJECT lever, POWER and RESET on the
+front deck; the RAM adapter lying on the back deck; the two controllers standing in their docks down its sides. The
+printing is one texture drawn by fds_print.py (the set from above, planar-mapped onto every face facing up; the front
+slope along it; the drive's front; the controllers' faces; the disk card's two sides; swatches).
+
+A node tree: a root (the turn to a three-quarter view, TILT_YAW and TILT_PITCH: the right side, with controller II,
+towards the viewer, the top tipped up; then the model spec's fit: standing on y = 0, centred, the largest side 1 m)
+holding the set; the set holding the disk card (waiting in the slot, shrunk to nothing), the eject button, the
+operating lamp (shrunk to nothing) and POWER.
+
+The `focused` clip (8 s, looping) plays a two-sided game: POWER slides on; the card slides into the drive, side A up,
+and the lamp flickers while it reads; the eject button goes in, the card pops out, turns over in the air and goes back
+in, side B up, and the lamp flickers again; then it's ejected and goes, and POWER slides off.
+
+Five materials (red, white, dark, base, print) and one texture, within the system model budget. Run from the repo
+root:
+
+    python tools/console-models/fds_print.py artifacts/fds
+    blender -b --factory-startup --python tools/console-models/fds.py -- artifacts/fds godot/themes/console/models/systems/fds.glb
+"""
+
+import math
+import os
+import sys
+
+import bmesh
+import bpy
+from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import fds_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+from amiga import paint, solid  # noqa: E402
+from clip import HIDDEN, Pose, back_out, ease_in, ease_out, key, phase, smooth  # noqa: E402
+from mega_drive_cartridge import bevel, boolean, box, export, join, material, new_object, prism_x, triangles  # noqa: E402
+
+TILT_YAW = -30.0     # degrees about the vertical: the right side comes towards the viewer
+TILT_PITCH = 24.0    # degrees about the horizontal: the top tips up towards the viewer
+ROUGHNESS = dict(red=0.45, white=0.5, dark=0.5, base=0.55, print=0.45)
+TOP_DEPTH = 250.0    # the top region's depth (fds_print.py's)
+FY, FZ = L.FAMICOM["y"], L.FAMICOM["z"]
+
+
+# ---- UVs -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def atlas_uv(region, w, h):
+    """A face drawn w x h into region: (a, b) millimetres across it (a to the right, b down from its top) to UVs."""
+    rx, ry, rw, rh = region
+    return lambda a, b: ((rx + a / w * rw) / L.ATLAS, 1 - (ry + b / h * rh) / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+TOP = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["top"], L.WIDTH, TOP_DEPTH)
+DRIVE_FACE = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["drive"], L.WIDTH, L.DRIVE["height"])
+
+
+def top_uv(co):
+    return TOP(co.x + L.WIDTH / 2, TOP_DEPTH - co.y)
+
+
+def drive_uv(co):
+    return DRIVE_FACE(co.x + L.WIDTH / 2, L.DRIVE["height"] - co.z)
+
+
+def swatch(name):
+    x, y = L.SWATCHES[name]
+    return lambda co: (x / L.ATLAS, 1 - y / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+def painted(obj, m, name):
+    paint(obj, m["print"], swatch(name), lambda c, n, _name: True)
+    return obj
+
+
+# ---- The drive -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def drive(m):
+    """The drive: the box, the seam round it, its front's panel, bay and slot; its front and top printed."""
+    w, d, h = L.WIDTH, L.DRIVE["depth"], L.DRIVE["height"]
+    shell = box("fds", -w / 2, w / 2, 0.0, d, 0.0, h, m["red"])
+    bevel(shell, L.DRIVE["r"], segments=3)
+    s = L.DRIVE["seam"]
+    ring = box("seam", -w / 2 - 5.0, w / 2 + 5.0, -5.0, d + 5.0, s - 0.6, s + 0.6, m["base"])
+    boolean(ring, box("inner", -w / 2 + 0.9, w / 2 - 0.9, 0.9, d - 0.9, s - 2.0, s + 2.0, m["base"]))
+    boolean(shell, ring)
+    p, b, sl = L.PANEL, L.BAY, L.SLOT
+    boolean(shell, box("panel", *p["x"], -5.0, p["depth"], *p["z"], m["dark"]))
+    boolean(shell, box("bay", *b["x"], -5.0, p["depth"] + b["depth"], *b["z"], m["dark"]))
+    boolean(shell, box("slot", *sl["x"], -5.0, sl["depth"], *sl["z"], m["dark"]))
+    paint(shell, m["print"], drive_uv, lambda c, n, name: n.y < -0.9 and c.y < p["depth"] + 0.3)
+    paint(shell, m["print"], top_uv, lambda c, n, name: n.z > 0.9 and c.z > h - 0.5)
+    return shell
+
+
+def eject_button(m):
+    e = L.EJECT
+    face = L.PANEL["depth"]
+    button = painted(box("eject", *e["x"], face - e["out"], face + 2.0, *e["z"], m["print"]), m, "yellow")
+    bevel(button, 0.6, segments=1)
+    return button
+
+
+def lamp(m):
+    """The operating lamp lit: a disc just over the printed one, its middle at its origin."""
+    x, z, r = L.LAMP
+    y = L.PANEL["depth"] - 0.15
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    ring = [bm.verts.new((r * 1.2 * math.cos(2 * math.pi * k / 12), 0.0, r * 1.2 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * k / 12)))
+            for k in range(12)]
+    bm.faces.new(ring)                                     # wound to face -y
+    lit = painted(new_object("lamp", bm, m["print"]), m, "lit")
+    return lit, Vector((x, y, z))
+
+
+# ---- The Famicom -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def place(obj):
+    """Moves a part built in the Famicom's frame (y from its front, z from its foot) to its place on the drive."""
+    obj.data.transform(Matrix.Translation((0.0, FY, FZ)))
+    return obj
+
+
+def band_uv():
+    """The front slope's UVs: across it, and down it from its top."""
+    (y0, z0), (y1, z1) = L.SLOPE
+    length = L.slope_length()
+    uv = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["band"], L.WIDTH, length)
+
+    def of(co):
+        y, z = co.y - FY, co.z - FZ
+        s = ((y - y1) * (y0 - y1) + (z - z1) * (z0 - z1)) / length
+        return uv(co.x + L.WIDTH / 2, s)
+    return of
+
+
+def on_slope(c, n):
+    (y0, z0), (y1, z1) = L.SLOPE
+    return n.y < -0.4 and n.z > 0.4 and z0 - 0.5 < c.z - FZ < z1 + 0.5 and c.y - FY < y1 + 0.5
+
+
+def famicom(m):
+    """The Famicom: the base, the shell, the EJECT lever, RESET, the RAM adapter, the controllers; printed."""
+    b = L.BASE
+    base = place(box("base", -b["x"], b["x"], 2.0, 218.0, 0.0, b["height"], m["base"]))
+    bevel(base, 1.5, segments=2)
+    shell = place(prism_x("famicom", L.shell_profile(), -74.0, 74.0, m["white"]))
+    bevel(shell, 1.5, segments=2)
+    paint(shell, m["print"], band_uv(), lambda c, n, name: on_slope(c, n))
+    paint(shell, m["print"], top_uv, lambda c, n, name: n.z > 0.5 and not on_slope(c, n))
+
+    lv = L.LEVER
+    lever = place(prism_x("lever", [(lv["y"][0], 35.0), (lv["y"][1], 37.0), (lv["y"][1], 52.0),
+                                    (lv["y"][1] - 9.0, lv["top"]), (lv["y"][0] + 7.0, lv["top"])],
+                          *lv["x"], m["red"]))
+    bevel(lever, 1.0, segments=2)
+    rx, ry = L.RESET["at"]
+    rw, rd, rh = L.RESET["size"]
+    reset = place(box("reset", rx - rw / 2, rx + rw / 2, ry - rd / 2, ry + rd / 2, 34.0, 36.0 + rh, m["red"]))
+    bevel(reset, 0.8, segments=1)
+    a = L.ADAPTER
+    adapter = place(box("adapter", *a["x"], *a["y"], 43.0, a["top"], m["dark"]))
+    bevel(adapter, 2.0, segments=2)
+    paint(adapter, m["print"], top_uv, lambda c, n, name: n.z > 0.9)
+    t = L.TAB
+    tab = place(box("tab", *t["x"], -t["out"], 3.0, *t["z"], m["red"]))
+    bevel(tab, 0.8, segments=1)
+
+    c = L.CONTROLLERS
+    pads = []
+    for side, region in ((-1, "pad1"), (1, "pad2")):
+        x0, x1 = (c["x"][0], c["x"][1]) if side > 0 else (-c["x"][1], -c["x"][0])
+        pad = place(box("controller", x0, x1, *c["y"], *c["z"], m["red"]))
+        bevel(pad, 3.0, segments=2)
+        face = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS[region], c["y"][1] - c["y"][0], c["z"][1] - c["z"][0])
+        (y0, y1), (z0, z1) = c["y"], c["z"]
+        if side > 0:                                       # seen from the right: the front to the left
+            uv = (lambda f: lambda co: f(co.y - FY - y0, z1 - (co.z - FZ)))(face)
+        else:                                              # seen from the left: the front to the right
+            uv = (lambda f: lambda co: f(y1 - (co.y - FY), z1 - (co.z - FZ)))(face)
+        paint(pad, m["print"], uv, lambda cc, n, name, s=side: n.x * s > 0.9)
+        pads.append(pad)
+    return [base, shell, lever, reset, adapter, tab] + pads
+
+
+def power_slider(m):
+    px, py = L.POWER["at"]
+    w, d, h = L.POWER["size"]
+    slider = box("power", -w / 2, w / 2, -d / 2, d / 2, -1.5, h - 1.5, m["red"])
+    bevel(slider, 0.8, segments=1)
+    deck_z = 34.0 + (py - L.DECK[0][0]) / (L.DECK[1][0] - L.DECK[0][0]) * 3.0
+    return slider, Vector((px, py + FY, deck_z + FZ))
+
+
+# ---- The disk card ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def disk(m):
+    """The disk card, its middle at its origin, lying flat, its window's end towards +y (into the slot), side A up."""
+    (w, l), t = L.DISK["size"], L.DISK["thickness"]
+    card = box("disk", -w / 2, w / 2, -l / 2, l / 2, -t / 2, t / 2, m["print"])
+    bevel(card, 0.5, segments=1)
+    side_a = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["side_a"], w, l)
+    side_b = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["side_b"], w, l)
+    paint(card, m["print"], lambda co: side_a(co.x + w / 2, l / 2 - co.y), lambda c, n, name: n.z > 0.9)
+    paint(card, m["print"], lambda co: side_b(w / 2 - co.x, l / 2 - co.y), lambda c, n, name: n.z < -0.9)
+    paint(card, m["print"], swatch("yellow"), lambda c, n, name: abs(n.z) <= 0.9)
+    return card
+
+
+# ---- The focused clip ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+OUT = 100.0          # how far in front of its seat the card waits: wholly out of the slot
+
+
+def appear(f, f0, f1):
+    return HIDDEN + (1 - HIDDEN) * back_out(phase(f, f0, f1)) if f >= f0 else HIDDEN
+
+
+def card(f):
+    if f < 10 or f >= 226:
+        return Pose(scale=HIDDEN)
+    if f < 20:
+        return Pose(y=-OUT, scale=appear(f, 10, 18))
+    if f < 102:
+        return Pose(y=-OUT * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 20, 36))))
+    if f < 110:
+        return Pose(y=-30.0 * back_out(phase(f, 102, 108)))
+    if f < 118:                                            # out, and up
+        t = smooth(phase(f, 110, 118))
+        return Pose(y=-30.0 - (OUT - 30.0) * t, z=30.0 * t)
+    if f < 136:                                            # turned over in the air: side B up
+        return Pose(y=-OUT, z=30.0, roll=180.0 * smooth(phase(f, 118, 136)))
+    if f < 144:
+        return Pose(y=-OUT, z=30.0 * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 136, 144))), roll=180.0)
+    if f < 206:
+        return Pose(y=-OUT * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 144, 160))), roll=180.0)
+    if f < 214:
+        return Pose(y=-30.0 * back_out(phase(f, 206, 212)), roll=180.0)
+    t = ease_out(phase(f, 214, 222))
+    return Pose(y=-30.0 - 40.0 * t, z=30.0 * t, roll=180.0, scale=max(HIDDEN, 1 - ease_in(phase(f, 218, 226))))
+
+
+def timeline(f):
+    reading = (38 <= f < 92 or 162 <= f < 198) and (f // 3) % 5 != 4
+    press = max(smooth(phase(f, f0, f0 + 2)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, f0 + 4, f0 + 7))) for f0 in (100, 204))
+    on = smooth(phase(f, 4, 8)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 230, 234)))
+    return {"disk": card(f), "lamp": Pose() if reading else Pose(scale=HIDDEN), "eject": Pose(y=2.0 * press),
+            "power": Pose(x=L.POWER["travel"] * on)}
+
+
+# ---- Main ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def main():
+    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
+    images, out = os.path.abspath(args[0]), os.path.abspath(args[1])
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
+    scene = bpy.context.scene
+    scene.render.fps = L.FPS
+    printed = bpy.data.images.load(os.path.join(images, "fds_print.png"))
+    colours = dict(L.COLOURS, print="#FFFFFF")
+    m = {n: material(n, colours[n], r, printed if n == "print" else None) for n, r in ROUGHNESS.items()}
+
+    whole = join([drive(m)] + famicom(m), "fds")
+    button = eject_button(m)
+    lit, lit_at = lamp(m)
+    slider, slider_at = power_slider(m)
+    card_ = disk(m)
+    for obj in [whole, button, slider, card_]:
+        for p in obj.data.polygons:
+            p.use_smooth = True
+        obj.data.set_sharp_from_angle(angle=math.radians(40))
+
+    # The node tree: the root (the view and the fit) holds the set; the set holds the moving parts at their places.
+    root = bpy.data.objects.new("fds_root", None)
+    scene.collection.objects.link(root)
+    whole.parent = root
+    sl = L.SLOT
+    (w, length), t = L.DISK["size"], L.DISK["thickness"]
+    seat = Vector(((sl["x"][0] + sl["x"][1]) / 2, -L.DISK["inside"] + length / 2, (sl["z"][0] + sl["z"][1]) / 2))
+    for part, where in ((lit, lit_at), (slider, slider_at), (card_, seat)):
+        part.parent = whole
+        part.location = where
+    button.parent = whole
+    nodes = {"disk": card_, "lamp": lit, "eject": button, "power": slider}
+
+    # The three-quarter view, then the spec's fit of the set at rest, as the root's transform.
+    tilt = Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(TILT_PITCH), 4, "X") @ Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(TILT_YAW), 4, "Z")
+    points = [tilt @ v.co for v in whole.data.vertices]
+    lo = Vector([min(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    hi = Vector([max(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    size = hi - lo
+    root.matrix_world = Matrix.Scale(1 / max(size), 4) @ Matrix.Translation((-(lo.x + hi.x) / 2, -(lo.y + hi.y) / 2,
+                                                                             -lo.z)) @ tilt
+
+    key("focused", nodes, timeline, L.LENGTH)
+    meshes = [whole, button, lit, slider, card_]
+    print(f"FDS: {sum(triangles(o.data) for o in meshes)} triangles ({triangles(whole.data)} the set), "
+          f"{len({mat.name for o in meshes for mat in o.data.materials})} materials, "
+          f"size {size.x:.1f} x {size.y:.1f} x {size.z:.1f} mm tilted, before the fit")
+    export([root] + meshes, out, animations=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""The Famicom Disk System's measurements, shared by fds_print.py (which draws its printing) and fds.py (which builds
+it). Plain Python: Blender's Python imports it too.
+
+The Family Computer (HVC-001), 150 x 220 x 60 mm, sitting on its Disk System's drive (HVC-022), 150 x 246 x 73 mm (both
+Nintendo's figures), the RAM adapter (HVC-023) in its cartridge slot, its two controllers in their docks. Millimetres:
+x from the set's middle (left to right), y back from the drive's front, z up from the table. The rest was measured from
+Evan-Amos's photographs on Wikimedia Commons (the Famicom on its drive, the drive alone, the Famicom alone and with its
+controller out, a disk card), scaled by their widths; the disk card is 76 x 90 mm.
+
+The drive: a red box in two halves, a seam round it, the black panel in its front (the disk's slot in its bay, the
+yellow eject button, Nintendo HVC-022 FAMILY COMPUTER DISK SYSTEM, the operating lamp, grooved ends). The Famicom on
+it, its front set back: the dark red base; the white shell, its front sloping up to the front deck (POWER, the EJECT
+lever, RESET) and stepping up behind it to the back deck, where the black RAM adapter lies in the slot; the
+controllers standing in their red docks down its sides, their gold faces outwards; FAMILY COMPUTER on the red band
+across the front slope.
+
+One texture (ATLAS square, REGIONS): `top` (the Famicom and the drive seen from above: the decks' printing, the RAM
+adapter's top; planar-mapped onto every face facing up), `band` (the front slope, along it), `drive` (the drive's
+front), `pad1` and `pad2` (the controllers' faces), `side_a` and `side_b` (the disk card's two sides: a made-up game,
+Odyssey), and swatches. A region is (x, y, width, height) in pixels.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+ATLAS = 1024
+
+# -- The drive -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+WIDTH = 150.0
+DRIVE = dict(depth=246.0, height=73.0, seam=37.0, r=4.0)
+PANEL = dict(x=(-70.0, 70.0), z=(6.0, 65.0), depth=2.0)    # the black panel sunk into its front
+BAY = dict(x=(-50.0, 38.0), z=(39.0, 60.0), depth=4.0)     # the slot's bay in it
+SLOT = dict(x=(-41.0, 37.0), z=(47.5, 51.5), depth=96.0)   # the disk's slot, deep enough for the whole card
+EJECT = dict(x=(11.0, 24.0), z=(30.0, 35.5), out=3.0)      # the yellow eject button
+LAMP = (51.0, 23.0, 1.6)                                   # the operating lamp: x, z, radius
+
+# -- The Famicom -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+FAMICOM = dict(y=20.0, depth=220.0, z=DRIVE["height"])     # its front (back from the drive's front) and its foot
+
+
+def shell_profile():
+    """The white shell's side outline, (y, z) from the Famicom's front and foot: the front slope, the front deck, the
+    step, the back deck."""
+    return [(0.0, 7.0), (220.0, 7.0), (220.0, 41.0), (217.0, 44.0), (100.0, 44.0), (96.0, 37.0), (28.0, 34.0),
+            (4.0, 11.0), (0.0, 8.5)]
+
+
+BASE = dict(x=74.0, height=7.5)                             # the dark red base under the shell
+SLOPE = ((4.0, 11.0), (28.0, 34.0))                         # the front slope: its foot and its top, (y, z)
+DECK = ((28.0, 34.0), (96.0, 37.0))                         # the front deck
+POWER = dict(at=(-36.0, 52.0), size=(16.0, 10.0, 5.0), travel=6.0)    # its middle (x, y from the front); w, d, h
+RESET = dict(at=(37.0, 42.0), size=(18.0, 15.0, 3.0))
+LEVER = dict(x=(-10.0, 10.0), y=(56.0, 84.0), top=56.0)    # the EJECT lever: a wedge up to its top
+CONTROLLERS = dict(y=(78.0, 206.0), z=(7.5, 57.5), x=(61.0, 76.0))     # in their docks: along, up, across (each side)
+ADAPTER = dict(x=(-56.0, 56.0), y=(98.0, 228.0), top=58.0, grooves=6)  # the RAM adapter on the back deck
+TAB = dict(x=(-26.0, -6.0), z=(1.0, 13.0), out=3.0)        # the expansion port's cover, at the base's front
+
+# -- The disk card ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+DISK = dict(size=(76.0, 90.0), thickness=3.0, inside=6.0)  # w, length; how much stays out of the slot once in
+
+COLOURS = dict(red="#B2202A", white="#EDE8DC", dark="#141416", base="#7A1A1E", yellow="#F3B700")
+
+REGIONS = dict(top=(0, 0, 400, 656), band=(408, 0, 400, 104), drive=(408, 112, 400, 196),
+               pad1=(408, 316, 400, 156), pad2=(408, 480, 400, 156), side_a=(816, 0, 208, 246),
+               side_b=(816, 254, 208, 246))
+SWATCHES = dict(red=(16, 680), white=(48, 680), dark=(80, 680), base=(112, 680), yellow=(144, 680), lit=(176, 680),
+                lamp_off=(208, 680), gold=(240, 680))
+
+FPS = 30
+LENGTH = 240                 # 8 s
+
+
+def slope_length():
+    (y0, z0), (y1, z1) = SLOPE
+    return math.hypot(y1 - y0, z1 - z0)

+"""The Famicom Disk System's printing, for the console theme's Famicom Disk System model (tools/console-models/fds.py).
+
+Draws its atlas, its regions as fds_layout.py places them, each in millimetres as the model's planar UVs map it: the
+set seen from above (the Famicom's front deck with POWER, EJECT and RESET and the warnings beside them, the RAM
+adapter's top with Nintendo's badge, FAMILY COMPUTER DISK SYSTEM and HVC-023, its grooves); the Famicom's front slope
+(FAMILY COMPUTER on the red band); the drive's front (Nintendo HVC-022 FAMILY COMPUTER DISK SYSTEM, the grooved ends,
+the operating lamp's box, イジェクト); the two controllers' faces (the gold plates, the D-pads, SELECT and START on I,
+VOLUME and the microphone on II, B and A); the disk card's two sides (a made-up game, Odyssey, side A and side B);
+and the swatches small parts take their colour from. Run it with the system Python (Pillow):
+
+    python tools/console-models/fds_print.py <out folder>
+
+It writes fds_print.png there.
+"""
+
+import os
+import sys
+
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import fds_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+from psp_print import ship, space  # noqa: E402
+from retro_pc_print import rgb, shade  # noqa: E402
+from windows_pc_print import FONTS, Region  # noqa: E402
+
+RED = rgb(L.COLOURS["red"])
+WHITE = rgb(L.COLOURS["white"])
+DARK = rgb(L.COLOURS["dark"])
+YELLOW = rgb(L.COLOURS["yellow"])
+GOLD = (196, 168, 112)
+GOLD_TEXT = (218, 196, 140)
+TOP_DEPTH = 250.0           # the top region's depth: the drive's front to the adapter's back
+JP = "msgothic.ttc"
+
+
+def slanted(reg, text, font, size, x, y, fill, shear=0.22, anchor="mm"):
+    layer = reg.layer()
+    f = ImageFont.truetype(FONTS + font, max(1, round(size * reg.sx)))
+    ImageDraw.Draw(layer).text(reg.p(x, y), text, font=f, fill=fill + (255,), anchor=anchor)
+    yc = reg.p(0, y)[1]
+    reg.over(layer.transform(layer.size, Image.AFFINE, (1, shear, -shear * yc, 0, 1, 0)))
+
+
+def nintendo(reg, x, y, size, fill, box=None):
+    """Nintendo's name in its racetrack outline (or on a filled one, box)."""
+    w, h = size * 3.6, size * 1.25
+    if box is not None:
+        reg.rect_(x - w / 2, y - h / 2, x + w / 2, y + h / 2, box, r=h / 2)
+    reg.rect_(x - w / 2, y - h / 2, x + w / 2, y + h / 2, None, r=h / 2, outline=fill, width=size * 0.09)
+    reg.text("Nintendo", "arialbd.ttf", size * 0.82, x, y + size * 0.03, fill)
+
+
+# ---- The set from above ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def top():
+    reg = Region(L.REGIONS["top"], L.WIDTH, TOP_DEPTH, RED)
+    fy = L.FAMICOM["y"]
+
+    def at(x, y):
+        """A point of the Famicom (x, y from its front) in the region's millimetres."""
+        return x + L.WIDTH / 2, TOP_DEPTH - (y + fy)
+    reg.rect_(*at(-74.0, 220.0), *at(74.0, 0.0), WHITE)
+    grey = shade(WHITE, -0.22)
+    for x, y, words in ((-33.0, 52.0, "POWER"), (37.0, 42.0, "RESET")):
+        reg.rect_(*at(x - 15.0, y + 11.0), *at(x + 15.0, y - 11.0), shade(WHITE, -0.04), r=1.0)
+        reg.text(words, "arialbd.ttf", 2.4, *at(x - 14.0 if x < 0 else x + 14.0, y + 13.0), grey,
+                 anchor="lm" if x < 0 else "rm")
+    reg.text("EJECT", "arialbd.ttf", 2.4, *at(0.0, 50.0), grey)
+    for x, y, lines in ((-32.0, 80.0, ("●カセットを抜き", "差しする時は、", "必ず本体の電源を", "切ってください。")),
+                        (36.0, 70.0, ("●リセットスイッチ", "を押すと、それまで", "記憶されていた", "得点が消去されます。"))):
+        reg.rect_(*at(x - 13.0, y + 12.0), *at(x + 13.0, y - 8.0), WHITE, outline=(80, 80, 80), width=0.25)
+        for k, line in enumerate(lines):
+            reg.text(line, JP, 2.2, *at(x - 12.0, y + 9.5 - 3.0 * k), (60, 60, 60), anchor="lm")
+        ax, ay = at(x, y - 12.0)
+        reg.poly([(ax - 4.0, ay - 2.0), (ax + 4.0, ay - 2.0), (ax, ay + 2.5)], (120, 120, 120))
+        reg.poly([(ax - 2.6, ay - 1.4), (ax + 2.6, ay - 1.4), (ax, ay + 1.4)], WHITE)
+
+    # The RAM adapter: black, its grooves at each end, Nintendo's badge, its names.
+    (ax0, ax1), (ay0, ay1) = L.ADAPTER["x"], L.ADAPTER["y"]
+    reg.rect_(*at(ax0, ay1), *at(ax1, ay0), DARK)
+    for k in range(L.ADAPTER["grooves"]):
+        for y in (ay0 + 5.0 + 3.0 * k, ay1 - 5.0 - 3.0 * k):
+            reg.line([at(ax0 + 2.0, y), at(ax1 - 2.0, y)], (44, 44, 48), 0.9)
+    reg.rect_(*at(8.0, 182.0), *at(52.0, 170.0), (230, 230, 230))
+    reg.text("Nintendo", "arialbd.ttf", 6.4, *at(30.0, 176.0), DARK)
+    slanted(reg, "FAMILY COMPUTER  DISK  SYSTEM", "arial.ttf", 2.6, *at(16.0, 160.0), (220, 220, 222), shear=0.0)
+    reg.rect_(*at(30.0, 154.5), *at(52.0, 149.5), (220, 220, 222))
+    reg.text("HVC-023", "arialbd.ttf", 3.4, *at(41.0, 152.0), DARK)
+    return reg
+
+
+def band():
+    length = L.slope_length()
+    reg = Region(L.REGIONS["band"], L.WIDTH, length, WHITE)
+    # The band runs up the slope: b from the slope's top (0) down to its foot (length).
+    reg.rect_(0.0, length * 0.32, L.WIDTH - 22.0, length * 0.92, RED)
+    for y in (length * 0.2, length * 0.96):
+        reg.line([(6.0, y), (L.WIDTH - 2.0, y)], GOLD_TEXT, 0.5)
+    slanted(reg, "FAMILY COMPUTER", "arialbd.ttf", 10.0, 70.0, length * 0.6, GOLD_TEXT, shear=0.24)
+    reg.text("™", "arial.ttf", 4.0, 118.0, length * 0.42, GOLD_TEXT)
+    slanted(reg, "Nintendo®", "arialbd.ttf", 4.0, 122.0, length * 0.82, GOLD_TEXT, shear=0.2)
+    return reg
+
+
+def drive():
+    reg = Region(L.REGIONS["drive"], L.WIDTH, L.DRIVE["height"], RED)
+
+    def at(x, z):
+        return x + L.WIDTH / 2, L.DRIVE["height"] - z
+    (px0, px1), (pz0, pz1) = L.PANEL["x"], L.PANEL["z"]
+    reg.rect_(*at(px0, pz1), *at(px1, pz0), DARK)
+    for x0, x1, z0, z1 in ((px0, px0 + 10.0, pz0, pz1), (px1 - 22.0, px1, pz0, pz0 + 18.0)):
+        for k in range(int((z1 - z0) / 2.4)):                 # the grooved ends
+            z = z0 + 1.2 + 2.4 * k
+            reg.line([at(x0 + 1.0, z), at(x1 - 1.0, z)], (40, 40, 44), 0.9)
+    lx, lz, _ = L.LAMP
+    reg.rect_(*at(px1 - 22.0, lz + 8.0), *at(px1 - 1.0, lz - 6.0), (20, 20, 22), outline=(44, 44, 48), width=0.4)
+    reg.circle(*at(lx, lz), L.LAMP[2], (70, 16, 16))
+    reg.text("◀作動中", JP, 3.0, *at(lx + 3.0, lz), (220, 220, 220), anchor="lm")
+    reg.text("Nintendo", "arialbd.ttf", 5.4, *at(-48.0, 30.0), (240, 240, 240), anchor="lm")
+    reg.rect_(*at(-48.0, 25.0), *at(-31.0, 20.6), (240, 240, 240))
+    reg.text("HVC-022", "arialbd.ttf", 3.6, *at(-39.5, 22.8), DARK)
+    reg.text("FAMILY COMPUTER  DISK  SYSTEM", "arial.ttf", 2.8, *at(-28.0, 14.0), (230, 230, 230), anchor="lm")
+    reg.text("イジェクト", JP, 2.6, *at(17.5, 26.0), (230, 230, 230))
+    return reg
+
+
+# ---- The controllers ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+PAD_W, PAD_H = 128.0, 50.0
+
+
+def pad_face(region, number):
+    """A controller's face, its cable's end to the left: the red border, the gold plate, the D-pad, the buttons."""
+    reg = Region(region, PAD_W, PAD_H, RED)
+    reg.rect_(4.0, 13.0 if number == 1 else 4.0, PAD_W - 4.0, PAD_H - 4.0, GOLD)
+    if number == 1:
+        reg.rect_(4.0, 4.0, 52.0, 13.0, GOLD)
+    for y in (PAD_H - 9.0, PAD_H - 7.6):
+        reg.line([(6.0, y), (PAD_W - 6.0, y)], (120, 30, 30), 0.35)
+    reg.rect_(8.0, 7.0 if number == 2 else 15.0, 14.0, 13.0 if number == 2 else 21.0, DARK)

+"""The console theme's Flash system model (godot/themes/console/models/systems/flash.glb): a 2000s LCD monitor playing
+a Flash game in a browser, and its mouse.
+
+Flash has no hardware (flash_layout.py): its card is a silver 17-inch LCD on its oval foot, the browser filling its
+screen, and a mouse beside it. The panel is its bezel (the screen's recess cut into its front) and the housing behind
+it; the neck rises from the foot to the housing; the buttons and the blue power light sit along the bezel's lower lip,
+the brand plate in its middle. The mouse is lofted from its outline, domed, its top printed. The printing is one
+texture drawn by flash_print.py: the screens, the plate, the mouse's top and swatches.
+
+A node tree: a root (the turn to a three-quarter view, TILT_YAW and TILT_PITCH; then the model spec's fit: standing on
+y = 0, centred, the largest side 1 m) holding the set; the set holding the screens over the glass (the preloader's
+bar filling, Odyssey's title, two frames of play, the right-click menu), shrunk to nothing, so at rest the card shows
+the preloader's splash with the Flash logo; and the mouse.
+
+The `focused` clip (8 s, looping) plays it: the preloader's bar fills, Odyssey's title comes up, the mouse moves and
+clicks PLAY (it dips under the finger), two frames of play take turns, a right click brings up the menu ending in About
+Adobe Flash Player, and the page loads again.
+
+Four materials (silver, black, glass, mouse) and one texture, within the system model budget. Run from the repo root:
+
+    python tools/console-models/flash_print.py artifacts/flash
+    blender -b --factory-startup --python tools/console-models/flash.py -- artifacts/flash godot/themes/console/models/systems/flash.glb
+"""
+
+import math
+import os
+import sys
+
+import bmesh
+import bpy
+from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import flash_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+from amiga import curved, paint, rounded, solid  # noqa: E402
+from clip import HIDDEN, Pose, key, phase, smooth  # noqa: E402
+from mega_drive_cartridge import bevel, boolean, box, export, join, material, new_object, triangles  # noqa: E402
+
+TILT_YAW = -24.0     # degrees about the vertical: the right side comes towards the viewer
+TILT_PITCH = 12.0    # degrees about the horizontal: the top tips back a little
+ROUGHNESS = dict(silver=0.35, black=0.5, glass=0.15, mouse=0.4)
+STATES = ("load", "title", "game1", "game2", "menu")
+
+
+def atlas_uv(region, w, h):
+    rx, ry, rw, rh = region
+    return lambda a, b: ((rx + a / w * rw) / L.ATLAS, 1 - (ry + b / h * rh) / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+def swatch(name):
+    x, y = L.SWATCHES[name]
+    return lambda co: (x / L.ATLAS, 1 - y / L.ATLAS)
+
+
+def painted(obj, mat, name):
+    paint(obj, mat, swatch(name), lambda c, n, _name: True)
+    return obj
+
+
+def ellipse(cx, cy, rx, ry, n=32):
+    return [(cx + rx * math.cos(2 * math.pi * k / n), cy + ry * math.sin(2 * math.pi * k / n)) for k in range(n)]
+
+
+# ---- The monitor -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+GLASS_Z = L.PANEL["bottom"] + L.PANEL["lip"] + L.GLASS[1] / 2     # the glass's middle's height
+
+
+def monitor(m):
+    """The panel (the bezel, the screen's recess, the housing behind), the neck, the foot, the buttons, the light, the
+    plate; the glass at rest."""
+    p = L.PANEL
+    w, h, b = p["width"], p["height"], p["bottom"]
+    bezel = solid("flash", [[(x, y, z) for x, z in rounded(0.0, b + h / 2, w, h, 10.0, 4)] for y in (0.0, 22.0)],
+                  m["silver"])
+    bevel(bezel, 2.0, segments=2)
+    gw, gh = L.GLASS
+    boolean(bezel, box("recess", -gw / 2 - 1.0, gw / 2 + 1.0, -5.0, 3.0, GLASS_Z - gh / 2 - 1.0, GLASS_Z + gh / 2 + 1.0,
+                       m["black"]))
+    housing = solid("housing", [[(x, y, z) for x, z in rounded(0.0, b + h * 0.55, wd, hd, 18.0, 4)] for y, wd, hd in
+                                ((20.0, w - 30.0, h - 40.0), (p["depth"], w * 0.62, h * 0.55))], m["silver"])
+    bevel(housing, 3.0, segments=2, angle=50)
+    s = L.STAND
+    nw, nd = s["neck"]
+    neck = box("neck", -nw / 2, nw / 2, s["neck_y"] - nd / 2, s["neck_y"] + nd / 2, 4.0, b + s["top"], m["silver"])
+    bevel(neck, 4.0, segments=2)
+    bw, bd, bh = s["base"]
+    foot = solid("foot", [[(x, y, z) for x, y in ellipse(0.0, s["base_y"], rx, ry, 48)] for rx, ry, z in
+                          ((bw / 2 - 4.0, bd / 2 - 4.0, 0.0), (bw / 2, bd / 2, 4.0), (bw / 2 - 10.0, bd / 2 - 10.0, bh))],
+                 m["silver"])
+    parts = [bezel, housing, neck, foot]
+    bx, bz = L.BUTTONS["x"], b + 12.0
+    for x in bx:
+        button = box("button", x - 4.0, x + 4.0, -1.2, 1.0, bz - 1.5, bz + 1.5, m["black"])
+        parts.append(button)
+    lx, lz, lr = L.LED
+    led = solid("led", [[(x, y, z) for x, z in ellipse(lx, b + 12.0, lr, lr, 12)] for y in (-1.0, 1.0)], m["black"])
+    parts.append(painted(led, m["glass"], "blue"))
+
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    layer = bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
+    pw, ph = 60.0, 9.0
+    corners = [(-pw / 2, b + 7.5), (pw / 2, b + 7.5), (pw / 2, b + 7.5 + ph), (-pw / 2, b + 7.5 + ph)]   # facing -y
+    face = bm.faces.new([bm.verts.new((x, -0.15, z)) for x, z in corners])
+    uv = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["plate"], pw, ph)
+    for loop, (x, z) in zip(face.loops, corners):
+        loop[layer].uv = uv(x + pw / 2, b + 7.5 + ph - z)
+    parts.append(new_object("plate", bm, m["glass"]))
+
+    glass = curved("glass", gw, gh, 0.0, atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["rest"], 1.0, 1.0), m["glass"], 8, 6)
+    glass.data.transform(Matrix.Translation((0.0, 2.6, GLASS_Z)))
+    parts.append(glass)
+    return parts
+
+
+def screens(m):
+    gw, gh = L.GLASS
+    return {name: curved("screen_" + name, gw, gh, 0.0, atlas_uv(L.REGIONS[name], 1.0, 1.0), m["glass"], 8, 6)
+            for name in STATES}
+
+
+# ---- The mouse -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def mouse(m):
+    """The mouse, its middle at its origin, its buttons towards +y: an egg lofted up to a dome, its top printed (the
+    buttons' seams, the wheel)."""
+    w, length, h = L.MOUSE["size"]
+    rings = []
+    for z, scale in ((0.0, 0.94), (3.0, 1.0), (h * 0.55, 0.97), (h * 0.8, 0.84), (h * 0.95, 0.6), (h, 0.3)):
+        rings.append([(x * scale, y * scale + (1 - scale) * 6.0, z) for x, y in egg(w, length)])
+    body = solid("mouse", rings, m["mouse"])
+    for poly in body.data.polygons:
+        poly.use_smooth = True
+    top = atlas_uv(L.REGIONS["mouse"], w, length)
+    paint(body, m["mouse"], lambda co: top(co.x + w / 2, length / 2 - co.y), lambda c, n, name: n.z > 0.3)
+    paint(body, m["mouse"], swatch("grey"), lambda c, n, name: n.z <= 0.3)
+    return body
+
+
+def egg(w, length, n=32):
+    """The mouse's outline: an egg, wider at the back (-y)."""
+    points = []
+    for k in range(n):
+        a = 2 * math.pi * k / n
+        y = length / 2 * math.sin(a)
+        x = w / 2 * math.cos(a) * (1.0 - 0.12 * math.sin(a))
+        points.append((x, y))
+    return points
+
+
+# ---- The focused clip ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def timeline(f):
+    shown = None
+    if 30 <= f < 60:
+        shown = "load"
+    elif 60 <= f < 100:
+        shown = "title"
+    elif 100 <= f < 164:
+        shown = "game1" if ((f - 100) // 8) % 2 == 0 else "game2"
+    elif 164 <= f < 206:
+        shown = "menu"
+    poses = {"screen_" + name: Pose() if name == shown else Pose(scale=HIDDEN) for name in STATES}
+    glide = smooth(phase(f, 66, 88)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 206, 230)))
+    nudge = smooth(phase(f, 150, 162)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, 206, 230)))
+    poses["mouse"] = Pose(x=10.0 * glide, y=8.0 * glide - 6.0 * nudge)
+    click = max(smooth(phase(f, f0, f0 + 2)) * (1 - smooth(phase(f, f0 + 4, f0 + 7))) for f0 in (92, 160))
+    poses["mouse"].offset.z -= 1.2 * click                    # a click: the mouse dips under the finger
+    poses["mouse"].squash = 0.04 * click
+    return poses
+
+
+# ---- Main ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def main():
+    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
+    images, out = os.path.abspath(args[0]), os.path.abspath(args[1])
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
+    scene = bpy.context.scene
+    scene.render.fps = L.FPS
+    printed = bpy.data.images.load(os.path.join(images, "flash_print.png"))
+    colours = dict(L.COLOURS)
+    textures = dict(glass=printed, mouse=printed)
+    m = {n: material(n, colours[n], r, textures.get(n)) for n, r in ROUGHNESS.items()}
+
+    whole = join(monitor(m), "flash")
+    for poly in whole.data.polygons:
+        poly.use_smooth = True
+    whole.data.set_sharp_from_angle(angle=math.radians(40))
+    glass = screens(m)
+    rodent = mouse(m)
+
+    root = bpy.data.objects.new("flash_root", None)
+    scene.collection.objects.link(root)
+    whole.parent = root
+    for k, part in enumerate(glass.values()):
+        part.parent = whole
+        part.location = Vector((0.0, 2.2 - 0.25 * k, GLASS_Z))
+    mx, my = L.MOUSE["at"]
+    rodent.parent = whole
+    rodent.location = Vector((mx, my, 0.0))
+    rodent.rotation_euler = (0.0, 0.0, math.radians(L.MOUSE["turn"]))
+    nodes = {**{"screen_" + k: v for k, v in glass.items()}, "mouse": rodent}
+
+    tilt = Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(TILT_PITCH), 4, "X") @ Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(TILT_YAW), 4, "Z")
+    rest = Matrix.Translation((mx, my, 0.0)) @ Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(L.MOUSE["turn"]), 4, "Z")
+    points = [tilt @ v.co for v in whole.data.vertices] + [tilt @ rest @ v.co for v in rodent.data.vertices]
+    lo = Vector([min(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    hi = Vector([max(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    size = hi - lo
+    root.matrix_world = Matrix.Scale(1 / max(size), 4) @ Matrix.Translation((-(lo.x + hi.x) / 2, -(lo.y + hi.y) / 2,
+                                                                             -lo.z)) @ tilt
+
+    key("focused", nodes, timeline, L.LENGTH)
+    meshes = [whole, rodent] + list(glass.values())
+    print(f"Flash: {sum(triangles(o.data) for o in meshes)} triangles ({triangles(whole.data)} the set), "
+          f"{len({mat.name for o in meshes for mat in o.data.materials})} materials, "
+          f"size {size.x:.1f} x {size.y:.1f} x {size.z:.1f} mm tilted, before the fit")
+    export([root] + meshes, out, animations=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Flash's card, a 2000s monitor playing a Flash game: the measurements shared by flash_print.py (which draws its
+printing and screens) and flash.py (which builds it). Plain Python: Blender's Python imports it too.
+
+Flash has no hardware: its games were played in a web browser, the Flash Player's red logo on their preloaders, its
+right-click menu ending in About Adobe Flash Player. The card is that: a silver 17-inch LCD monitor of the time on its
+oval foot, a browser window filling its screen with a Flash game in the page (a made-up game, Odyssey), and a mouse
+beside its foot. Millimetres: x from the monitor's middle (left to right), y back from its panel's front, z up from the
+table. A 17-inch 4:3 panel's active area is 338 x 270 mm; the rest is typical of the monitors of the time.
+
+The Flash logo (F_LOGO) is the white f traced from the Flash Player icon on Wikimedia Commons, normalised to its
+square (x right, y down, 0 to 1).
+
+One texture (ATLAS square, REGIONS): the screens, each the glass's whole area (`rest`, the preloader's splash with the
+Flash logo; `load`, its bar filling; `title`, Odyssey's title with the pointer on PLAY; `game1` and `game2`, two frames
+of play; `menu`, the right-click menu over the game), the brand plate under the screen, the mouse's top, and swatches.
+A region is (x, y, width, height) in pixels.
+"""
+
+ATLAS = 1024
+
+PANEL = dict(width=370.0, height=306.0, depth=52.0, bottom=92.0, bezel=16.0, lip=24.0)   # the bezel; the deeper bottom
+GLASS = (338.0, 270.0)
+STAND = dict(base=(240.0, 196.0, 16.0), base_y=70.0, neck=(70.0, 30.0), neck_y=96.0, top=150.0)
+LED = (156.0, -14.0, 2.2)                                   # the power light: x, z from the panel's bottom edge, radius
+BUTTONS = dict(x=[96.0 + 13.0 * k for k in range(4)], z=-12.0, size=(8.0, 3.0))   # under the screen, at the right
+
+MOUSE = dict(at=(196.0, -62.0), turn=-12.0, size=(64.0, 116.0, 36.0), split=50.0)   # w, length, h; buttons' length
+
+F_LOGO = [(0.742, 0.179), (0.761, 0.179), (0.761, 0.307), (0.714, 0.312), (0.693, 0.319), (0.664, 0.338),

+          (0.477, 0.703), (0.434, 0.752), (0.384, 0.788), (0.351, 0.804), (0.318, 0.815), (0.273, 0.823),
+          (0.242, 0.824), (0.242, 0.697), (0.283, 0.692), (0.320, 0.678), (0.346, 0.659), (0.373, 0.627),
+          (0.410, 0.557), (0.463, 0.422), (0.497, 0.347), (0.518, 0.312), (0.545, 0.276), (0.583, 0.238),
+          (0.636, 0.205), (0.694, 0.186)]
+
+COLOURS = dict(silver="#B8BBC0", black="#121214", glass="#FFFFFF", mouse="#C9CBCF", dark="#2A2B2E")
+
+SCREEN_PX = (400, 320)
+REGIONS = dict(rest=(0, 0) + SCREEN_PX, load=(408, 0) + SCREEN_PX, title=(0, 328) + SCREEN_PX,
+               game1=(408, 328) + SCREEN_PX, game2=(0, 656) + SCREEN_PX, menu=(408, 656) + SCREEN_PX,

+"""Flash's card's screens and printing, for the console theme's Flash model (tools/console-models/flash.py).
+
+Draws its atlas, its regions as flash_layout.py places them: the screens, each a browser window of the 2000s filling
+the glass (its blue title bar, its menus, the address bar, the page with a Flash game in it, the status bar), the game
+in its states (the preloader's splash with the Flash logo, its bar filling; Odyssey's title, the pointer on PLAY; two
+frames of play; the right-click menu ending in About Adobe Flash Player); the brand plate under the screen; the mouse's
+top; and the swatches small parts take their colour from. Odyssey and the site it's on (odyssey.example, a domain kept
+for examples) are made up. Run it with the system Python (Pillow):
+
+    python tools/console-models/flash_print.py <out folder>
+
+It writes flash_print.png there.
+"""
+
+import os
+import random
+import sys
+
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import flash_layout as L  # noqa: E402
+from psp_print import ship, space  # noqa: E402
+from retro_pc_print import rgb  # noqa: E402
+from windows_pc_print import FONTS, gradient  # noqa: E402
+
+SS = 3                       # the screens drawn this many times larger, then resampled
+W, H = L.SCREEN_PX
+MOVIE = (40, 74, 360, 290)   # the Flash movie in the page: x0, y0, x1, y1
+
+
+def font(name, size):
+    return ImageFont.truetype(FONTS + name, max(1, round(size * SS)))
+
+
+def box(x0, y0, x1, y1):
+    return [x0 * SS, y0 * SS, x1 * SS, y1 * SS]
+

+"""The console theme's Game & Watch system model (godot/themes/console/models/systems/gameandwatch.glb): a Game & Watch
+Multi Screen, open on the table, a made-up game on its two screens.
+
+Built in Blender from the real handheld's proportions (gameandwatch_layout.py has the measurements, taken from
+photographs). Each half is a slab, its edges rounded, its face printed; the lower half lies on the table, the D-pad,
+GAME A, GAME B, TIME and JUMP standing on its face; the upper half turns on the hinges along the lower half's back edge,
+open, its title plate and side panels printed. The printing is one texture drawn by gameandwatch_print.py: the two
+faces (each with its screen at rest: the clock), the screens while the game's played, and swatches.
+
+A node tree: a root (the turn to a three-quarter view, TILT_YAW and TILT_PITCH: the right end towards the viewer, the top
+tipped up; then the model spec's fit: standing on y = 0, centred, the largest side 1 m) holding the lower half; the
+lower half holding the D-pad, GAME A, JUMP, three screens over its screen and the upper half (its origin on the hinge);
+the upper half holding three screens over its own.
+
+The `focused` clip (8 s, looping) plays a game: GAME A is pressed; the rocks fall down the top screen while the ship
+dodges along the bottom one, the D-pad rocking left and right, JUMP firing; then the game ends, the handheld shuts with
+a snap and springs open again, back to the clock.
+
+Four materials (case, key, glass, print) and one texture, within the system model budget. Run from the repo root:
+
+    python tools/console-models/gameandwatch_print.py artifacts/gameandwatch
+    blender -b --factory-startup --python tools/console-models/gameandwatch.py -- artifacts/gameandwatch godot/themes/console/models/systems/gameandwatch.glb

+    upper.parent = lower
+    upper.location = (0.0, D, T)
+    upper.rotation_euler = (math.radians(L.OPEN), 0.0, 0.0)
+    for part, where in upper_screens.values():
+        part.parent = upper
+        part.location = where
+    nodes = {"upper": upper, **{n: p for n, (p, _) in parts.items()}, **{n: p for n, (p, _) in lower_screens.items()},
+             **{n: p for n, (p, _) in upper_screens.items()}}
+
+    # The three-quarter view, then the spec's fit of the open handheld at rest, as the root's transform.
+    tilt = Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(TILT_PITCH), 4, "X") @ Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(TILT_YAW), 4, "Z")
+    hinge = Matrix.Translation((0.0, D, T)) @ Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(L.OPEN), 4, "X")
+    points = [tilt @ v.co for v in lower.data.vertices] + [tilt @ hinge @ v.co for v in upper.data.vertices]
+    lo = Vector([min(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    hi = Vector([max(p[i] for p in points) for i in range(3)])
+    size = hi - lo
+    root.matrix_world = Matrix.Scale(1 / max(size), 4) @ Matrix.Translation((-(lo.x + hi.x) / 2, -(lo.y + hi.y) / 2,
+                                                                             -lo.z)) @ tilt
+
+    key("focused", nodes, timeline, L.LENGTH)
+    meshes = ([lower, upper] + [p for p, _ in parts.values()] + [p for p, _ in lower_screens.values()]
+              + [p for p, _ in upper_screens.values()])
+    print(f"Game & Watch: {sum(triangles(o.data) for o in meshes)} triangles ({triangles(lower.data)} the lower half), "
+          f"{len({mat.name for o in meshes for mat in o.data.materials})} materials, "
+          f"size {size.x:.1f} x {size.y:.1f} x {size.z:.1f} mm tilted, before the fit")
+    export([root] + meshes, out, animations=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""The Game & Watch's measurements, shared by gameandwatch_print.py (which draws its printing and screens) and
+gameandwatch.py (which builds it). Plain Python: Blender's Python imports it too.
+
+A Game & Watch Multi Screen (1982) in the brown and cream of Donkey Kong II, open on the table, a made-up game on its
+two screens: Odyssey. Each half is 122 x 74 mm and 12.5 mm thick (the Digital Game Museum's 4 3/4 x 3 x 1 inches for
+the closed handheld). Millimetres: x from its middle (left to right), y back from the lower half's front edge, z up from
+the table; on each half's face, u across from its middle and v from its front edge (the lower half's) or from the hinge
+(the upper half's). The rest was measured from photographs of a Donkey Kong II on Wikimedia Commons (from above, from in
+front, open at an angle), scaled by its width.
+
+The lower half: its brown body, its face cream with the brown panels at its sides: GAME & WATCH and the D-pad
+(CONTROLLER) at the left, GAME A, GAME B and TIME with ALARM and ACL, and JUMP at the right; the screen in the middle,
+the Nintendo plate under it. The upper half, hinged at the lower half's back edge, open: its face cream, the title
+plate over its screen, the raised panels at its sides, four screws; the ribbon between the halves.
+
+One texture (ATLAS square, REGIONS): `lower` and `upper` (the two faces, each with its screen at rest: the clock on the
+lower one), the screens while the game's played (`lower_1` to `lower_3`, `upper_1` to `upper_3`: an LCD's black
+segments over its printed backdrop), and swatches. A region is (x, y, width, height) in pixels.
+"""
+
+ATLAS = 1024
+
+WIDTH, DEPTH, HALF = 122.0, 74.0, 12.5               # each half: w x d, its thickness
+OPEN = -115.0                                         # the upper half's angle from shut, about the hinge
+
+# The lower half's face, (u, v): v from its front edge.
+LOWER_LCD = dict(at=(-1.0, 39.0), size=(54.0, 35.0))
+DPAD = dict(at=(-46.0, 23.0), size=16.0, arm=5.6, height=2.6)
+SMALL = dict(game_a=(41.5, 63.0), game_b=(41.5, 54.5), time=(41.5, 46.0), size=(7.4, 3.4), height=1.6)
+LIGHTS = dict(alarm=(49.5, 58.0), acl=(49.5, 50.5))
+JUMP = dict(at=(43.5, 23.0), r=4.8, height=2.4)
+BADGE = dict(at=(-46.0, 57.0), size=(14.0, 10.0))
+NINTENDO = dict(at=(-1.0, 12.0), size=(31.0, 6.0))
+PANELS = dict(left=(-58.0, -33.0), right=(33.0, 58.0))   # the brown side panels, u
+
+# The upper half's face, (u, v): v from the hinge.
+UPPER_LCD = dict(at=(0.2, 34.6), size=(56.0, 37.0))
+TITLE = dict(at=(0.0, 61.0), size=(31.0, 6.0))
+SCREWS = [(-30.0, 59.0), (30.0, 59.0), (-43.0, 10.0), (43.0, 10.0)]
+SIDE = dict(left=(-56.0, -34.0), right=(34.0, 56.0), v=(4.0, 70.0))   # the raised side panels
+
+COLOURS = dict(case="#6A3424", key="#141416", glass="#FFFFFF", print="#FFFFFF")
+
+SCREEN_PX = (184, 120)
+REGIONS = dict(lower=(0, 0, 640, 388), upper=(0, 396, 640, 388),
+               lower_1=(648, 0) + SCREEN_PX, lower_2=(840, 0) + SCREEN_PX, lower_3=(648, 128) + SCREEN_PX,
+               upper_1=(840, 128) + SCREEN_PX, upper_2=(648, 256) + SCREEN_PX, upper_3=(840, 256) + SCREEN_PX)
+SWATCHES = dict(brown=(664, 400), cream=(696, 400), dark=(728, 400), lit=(760, 400), metal=(792, 400))
